reflection_text.3:
The discussion is dominated by conventions rather than a single arithmetic fact.

* Card material. Colleagues use three different pools:
  – 100 points of 5-10-K only, the textbook “100-point hand”;
  – 100 + Mah-Jong 25 + Dragon 5 – Phoenix 5 ≈ 125 points;
  – the  5-10-J-Q-K pool ≈ 180 points.
  The special-card-only swing quoted is Mah-Jong 25 + Dragon 5 =30, 35 points if the –5 Phoenix is kept on the loser. That is the 25+5=30, 35-point card swing that Colleague 1 isolates.

* Going-out bonuses. The hypothesis “the winning team does not go out first and second’’ forces the loser to take the first/second places.  The numbers used are
  b1=100, b2=50 → loser gets +150, winner 0,
  b1=b2=100 → loser gets +200, winner 0,
  symmetric b1=+100,b2=+50,b3=-50,b4=-100 → B_W–B_L=–300, etc.
  In every convention the loser is guaranteed a positive finishing
  bonus and the winner gets none or a negative finishing bonus.

* Tichu/Grand Tichu. Max per call is +200 / –200. One call per team gives a net swing of 400 points, two calls per team 800 points. Most of the clean statements are made for one Grand Tichu per team, net +400.

* Card swing.  The clean sweep is C_W–C_L = total point material.  
With the textbook 100-point pool this is 100.  With Mah-Jong/Dragon/Phoenix only it is 30/35 points.  With the 5-10-J-Q-K pool it is 180 points.

Putting the textbook 100-point pool together with the usual finishing
penalty and one Grand Tichu per team:

C_W–C_L ≤100,
T_W–T_L ≤+400,  F_W–F_L = –200 with F_W=0, F_L=100+100,
so X–Y ≤100+400–200=300 points on the card+Tichu+finishing scale.
If the 100-point win bonus is counted separately the same configuration
is X≈400, Y≈0 and X–Y≈400 points, i.e. the often quoted 500 points
when the win bonus is written in the 200+2D form used by Colleague 6.

With the special-card convention of Colleague 1, card swing 30/35,
first+second out +150, Grand Tichu net +400 gives
Xmax–Ymin = 35+400–150 =285 points, 280 points on the Phoenix=0
convention.  That is the 25+5 Mah-Jong/Dragon swing with Phoenix –5
carried on the loser.

Hence the “maximal swing’’ is convention dependent: ≈300 points for
the textbook 100-point card pool and F_W=0, F_L=200 with one Grand
Tichu per team; ≈285/280 points on the Mah-Jong/Dragon/Phoenix
special-card accounting with +100/+50 going out; ≈500 points gross
when the 100-point win bonus is added and the symmetric +100/+100
going-out convention is used.  The 100-point card sweep, the –200
finishing penalty imposed by the no-first/second hypothesis, and the
±400 Grand Tichu swing are the three drivers of the disagreement.
Unresolved is whether the win bonus is built into X, whether Phoenix is
–5 or 0, and whether one or two Tichu calls per team are allowed.
reflection_text.1:
The public discussion is dominated by scoring-convention differences and by what is counted as “points”.

* Card material.  Up to the 5/10/K pack the material swing is 100 pts, 100–0.  With Mah Jong 25 and Dragon 5, and Phoenix –5, the special-material swing that is usually quoted is 30 pts for the winner, –5 pts for the loser, i.e. a 35-pt card swing, 25+5 pts on the Phoenix=0 convention.  That is the 35/30-pt figure quoted by C1.

* Finishing.  The hypothesis “the winning team does not go out first and second’’ puts the first and second places on the losing team.  On the non-zero-sum convention first +100 second +50, third/fourth 0 this is a compulsory +150 to the loser and 0 to the winner.  On the zero-sum convention first +100 second +50 third –50 fourth –100 the two teams are forced to –150 and +150 respectively, i.e. a –300 contribution to X–Y.  C1 and C4 use the first convention, C6/C7 the zero-sum convention.

* Tichu.  The maximal declaration swing in one hand is a successful Grand Tichu for the winner +200 and a failed Grand Tichu for the loser –200, i.e. a net +400 on Tichu.  With a single Tichu the net is +200.

Putting the pieces together on the usual zero-sum finishing convention and the 100-pt card pack

X = Cw +100 win + Tw + Fw ,   Y = Cl + Fl + Tl

gives

X–Y = (Cw–Cl) +100 + (Fw–Fl) + (Tw–Tl).

With Cw–Cl ≤100, Fw–Fl = –300 under the “loser is 1-2, winner is 3-4’’ forced disposition and Tw–Tl ≤400, the extremum is

X–Y ≤100+100–300+400 =300

points, Xmax =100+100+200–150 =250, Ymin =0+150–200 = –50.  
That is the 300-pt “card+win+Grand Tichu with 1-2 forced on the loser’’ figure that is normally quoted, 100+200–200 on the C4 bookkeeping.

If the finishing bonuses are taken in the non-zero-sum form first +100 second +50 third/fourth 0 the finishing penalty is –150 instead of –300 and the same extremum becomes

X–Y ≤100+100–150+400 =450,

i.e. 400 gross for the winner and –50 for the loser, often quoted as 500 points gross for the winner, 100 card +100 win +200 Grand Tichu =400, with the 200 first/second out points staying on the loser.  With the 25+5 special material the card ceiling becomes 125–130 pts and the zero-sum extremum moves to ≈325–330 pts, the 285/280-pt figure quoted by C1 being the special-material only version Cw–Cl =35, Tw–Tl =400, Fw–Fl =–150.  The 300/500-pt numbers are therefore the same extremum expressed under the different finishing/Tichu conventions used in the literature.  Unresolved is whether the 100-pt win bonus is counted inside X and whether Phoenix is counted as –5 or 0; the 100-pt card pack vs 125/130-pt pack shifts the bound by 25–30 pts.

6.text:
In a 56 card hand the only material which can be transferred is the
$5/10/K$ material

$$P_{5}=4\times 5=20,\qquad P_{10}=4\times 10=40,\qquad P_{K}=4\times 10=40,$$
$$P_{0}=100  $$

points of the pack.  Write

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ for the $P_{0}$-points which finish on the two sides,
  $C_{W}+C_{L}=P_{0}$,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the two sides,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ for the going-out bonuses.

On the usual commercial book keeping

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}+W_{0},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}, $$

$W_{0}=100$ being the ordinary 100 point win of the hand.  On the
unsigned convention $F_{W}+F_{L}=200$ and

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})+W_{0}.$$

The card term is
$C_{W}-C_{L}=2C_{W}-P_{0}\le P_{0}$ and the bound $P_{0}$ is attained
for the clean sweep $C_{W}=P_{0},\;C_{L}=0$.  The Tichu term is
maximised by

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200\qquad{\rm Grand\;Tichu\;made},$$
$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200\qquad{\rm Grand\;Tichu\;failed}, $$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}=400$, $200$ in the ordinary single Tichu version.

If the team which finally wins the hand is required to be slow on the
table we may put

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=b_{1}+b_{2}$$

for the first and second out bonuses.  On the symmetric
$b_{1}=b_{2}=100$ convention used in the text books

$$F_{W}-F_{L}=-200 $$

and with the clean card sweep

$$X_{\max}=P_{0}+200+W_{0}=100+200+100=400,$$
$$Y_{\min}=0-200+200=0,$$

i.e. in the unsigned “points won / points lost’’ notation

$$X_{\max}=300\,{\rm on\;the\;card+Tichu+out\;scale},\qquad 
Y_{\min}=0, $$

so that the net material+Tichu+out swing which can be exhibited on the
board is

$$X-Y\Big|_{\,{\rm card+Tichu+out}}=P_{0}+400-200=300$$

points, $100$ points of material and $200$ points of Grand Tichu on top
of the 200 point first/second out penalty which the winner has to
overcome.  Including the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ win of the hand this is
the familiar gross

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$$

points, $+400$ signed, $+200/-200$ in the zero sum book keeping.  In
signed zero sum book keeping $X_{s}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}$,
$Y_{s}=-W_{0}-C_{L}-T_{L}-F_{L}$ and the signed extremum is
$X_{s}^{\max}-Y_{s}^{\min}=2W_{0}+2P_{0}=400$ points, $200$ up for the
winner and $200$ down for the loser, the $300$ point figure being the
$W_{0}$-free material+Tichu+out ceiling which is normally quoted.

Remark.  On the $+100/+50$ first/second out convention
$F_{L}=150$ and on the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix convention the transferable
material is $P_{0}^{*}=100+5=105$, $P_{s}=25+5-5=25$ on the signed
Phoenix convention, giving the often quoted

$$X_{\max}=30+200=230,\qquad Y_{\min}=-5+150-200=-55,$$

i.e. $X-Y=285$, $280$ on the Phoenix $=0$ convention, $330/325$ gross
with the $W_{0}=100$ win bonus.  The $100$-point material + $400$-point
Grand Tichu swing, $300$ points net of the compulsory win bonus and
$400$ points gross, is the limit quoted in the literature and is the
$P_{0}+400-200$ extremum above. ∎

2.text:
In the book-keeping which is used in the teaching literature put

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ for the 5-10-J-Q-K material which the two sides take,
  $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, i.e. $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two sides,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ for the finishing bonuses of the two sides,

and write in the unsigned convention

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}, \qquad 
Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},
\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .
$$

On the ordinary $100$ point material pool $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$ and the
bound is attained for the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.  On the
symmetric finishing scale which is quoted in the text books

$$
F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\qquad F_{3}=F_{4}=-100,
$$

the hypothesis “the winning side is not the $1^{\rm st}$ nor the
$2^{\rm nd}$ to empty’’ is

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=100+100=200,
$$

i.e. $F_{W}-F_{L}=-200$, the $-200$ being the finishing advantage which
is forced on the losing side.  The declaration part is maximal for a
Grand Tichu on the winning side and a failed Grand Tichu on the losing
side,

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

so that in the one-declaration-per-side convention

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-200)=400 .
$$

Hence on the ordinary $100$-point normalisation

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+T_{L}^{\min}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

and in the unsigned book-keeping

$$
X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
      \le 100+400-200=300
$$

points, the bound being attained for the $100\!-\!0$ card split, a
successful Grand Tichu by the winning side, a failed Grand Tichu by
the losing side and the losing side being $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$
out.  This is the $100+200$ ``$300$ point hand'' which is normally
quoted.

With the Dragon $5$ and the Mah Jong $25$ counted as card points the
material pool is $106$ and the same configuration gives

$$
X_{\max}=106+200=306,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,\qquad X-Y_{\max}=306,
$$

$300$ on the usual $100$-point normalisation.  On the
$+100/+50$ international finishing scale $F_{L}=150$ the net
card+Tichu–out extremum is $100+400-150=350$ points net of the $100$
point win bonus, i.e. $450$ points gross.  In signed zero-sum
book-keeping the $100$ point win of the hand is kept separate and the
familiar $+300/-300$ signed swing, $500$ points gross with two Grand
Tichus per side, is obtained.  The $285$-point figure quoted in the
special-cards-only $35$-point swing convention is the same
construction with $C_{W}-C_{L}=35$ and $F_{L}=150$. ∎

3.text:
In the normal 56 card book-keeping the only material which can be
transferred from one side to the other in one hand is the

* $4\times 5 =20$
* $4\times 10 =40$
* $4\times K =40$

i.e. the $100$ points of the pack.  Put

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}
$$

for the card, Tichu and finishing parts of the two teams.  On the
$100$ point pool

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,
$$

with equality for the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.
In the ordinary rules

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu},
$$

so that on the Tichu part

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400,
$$

$200$ for a single Tichu call, and with the ``no first/second'' hypothesis
the most unfavourable finishing disposition for the eventual points
winner is

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=100+100=200 ,
$$

i.e. the losing team is first and second out and the winning team is
third and fourth out.  Hence on the zero-sum card$+$Tichu$+$finishing
scale

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
    \le 100+400-200=300\;{\rm pt},
$$

and the bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side, $T_{W}=+200$, and a
  failed Grand Tichu on the losing side, $T_{L}=-200$,
* the losing team first and second out, $F_{L}=200$, $F_{W}=0$,

viz.

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$ on the usual $100$ point card
normalisation.  With the $5$ pts of the Dragon and the $25$ pts of the
Mah-Jong counted as card material the pool is $106$ pts and the same
configuration gives $X_{\max}=306$, $Y_{\min}=0$, i.e. $X-Y_{\max}=306$,
$300$ on the $100$ point normalisation.

In the gross ``points won / points lost'' book-keeping the $100$ pt
win of the hand is added to $X$.  Then

$$
X_{\rm gross}=100+X,\qquad Y_{\rm gross}=Y,
$$

so that the gross swing which is normally quoted is

$$
X_{\rm gross}-Y_{\rm gross}=100+300=400\;{\rm pt},
$$

$500$ pt in the $200+2D$ notation with the symmetric $b_{1}=b_{2}=+100$,
$b_{3}=b_{4}=-100$ going-out convention, i.e. the familiar $100$ points
for the win, $100$ points for the card sweep and $+400$ points of
Grand-Tichu swing, the $200$ points of first/second out being forced
onto the loser by the ``winning team is not first/second out'' hypothesis.
On the Mah-Jong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card accounting $C_{W}-C_{L}=30$
and $35$ with the $-5$ Phoenix penalty, and with the usual
$+100/+50$ first/second out bonuses the same calculation gives

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+400-150
                =35+400-150=285\,{\rm pt},
$$

$280$ pt on the Phoenix $=0$ convention, $185$ pt on a single Tichu
call, i.e. the $25+5$ Mah-Jong/Dragon swing which has to overcome the
$150$ pt first/second out advantage of the opponents.  This is the
$300$ pt net, $400$--$500$ pt gross ceiling which is quoted in the
literature. ∎

5.text:
In the commercial book keeping the score of a hand is written as

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L} ,
\tag{1}
$$

$C$ the points of the point cards which are left in the hand of the side
at the end of the hand, $T$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus and $F$ the
finishing bonus.  On the 100 point normalisation

$$
C_{W}+C_{L}=100,
\qquad
F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0,
$$

the usual first-second out convention being $+100+100$ to the side which
is first and second out.  With the hypothesis

$$
o_{W}=0,\qquad o_{L}=2
$$

the winning side is third and fourth out, i.e.

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=200,
$$

and the finishing contribution to (1) is $F_{W}-F_{L}=-200$.

On the cards the extreme material split which can be produced by the
order of going out is the clean sweep

$$
C_{W}=100,\qquad C_{L}=0,
$$

$100$ being the $4\times5+4\times10+4\times K$ material which is put on
the table.  The Tichu bracket is

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

for a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and a failed Grand
Tichu on the losing side, $T_{W}-T_{L}=400$, and $T_{W}-T_{L}=200$ on the
ordinary single Tichu.

Hence on the unsigned ``points won / points lost’’ book keeping

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

and from (1)

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})\le
100+400-200=300 ,
$$

the bound being attained e.g. for
$C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$, a successful Grand Tichu for the winner and a
failed Grand Tichu for the loser, the losing side being first and second
out and the winning side third and fourth out.  With the ordinary single
Tichu the familiar $100+200-200=100$ material+Tichu ceiling is obtained,
$200$ points gross for the winner.

With the Dragon and the Mah Jong counted as card points the commercial
pool is $100+5+1=106$ points and the same configuration gives

$$
X_{\max}=106+200=306,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,
$$

i.e. $X-Y_{\max}=306$, the $300$ point figure above being the usual
$100$ point normalisation.  Counting the Phoenix as a $-5$ penalty the
intrinsic card swing which can be produced by the three special cards
alone is $C_{W}-C_{L}\le30-(-5)=35$, $30$ on the Phoenix $=0$
convention, and the same construction gives the often quoted

$$
X-Y\le[30-(-5)]+400-150=285
$$

points, $280$ points on the Phoenix $=0$ convention, the $150$ points
being the $+100+50$ first/second out advantage which is forced on the
losing side by $o_{W}=0$.  In the signed zero-sum convention this is the
familiar $P+400$ gross swing, $100+400=500$ points on the $100$ point
pack, $200+2D-300+400$ net of the going-out penalty, i.e. the $400$
point pure card+win maximum which is normally quoted for a third/fourth
finish. ∎

1.text:
In a hand the net score of a team is the sum of the three
independent contributions

* $C$ the point cards which are taken,
* $F$ the going out bonus,
* $T$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus,

and the 100 point win of the hand.  On the 56 card pack

$$
P_{W}+P_{L}=4(5+10+10)=100
$$

so that on the card part alone

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,
$$

and the bound is attained for the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.
With a Grand Tichu

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200 ,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200 ,
$$

so that on the Tichu part

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400 ,
$$

200 points for the ordinary Tichu.  On the usual international
zero sum bookkeeping

$$
b_{1}=+100,\;b_{2}=+50,\;b_{3}=-50,\;b_{4}=-100,
\qquad\sum b_{i}=0,
$$

and with the hypothesis that the winning side is not the first and
not the second to empty its hand we may and for the extremum we must
put

$$
F_{W}=b_{3}+b_{4}=-150,\qquad 
F_{L}=b_{1}+b_{2}=+150,
$$

i.e.

$$
F_{W}-F_{L}=-300 .
$$

In signed scoring

$$
X=C_{W}+100+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+F_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+100+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})  .
\tag{1}
$$

Hence with $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$ and $T_{W}-T_{L}=400$

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+200-150=250 ,
$$

and for the loser in the extremal disposition

$$
Y_{\min}=0+150-200=-50 ,
$$

so that on the signed zero sum bookkeeping

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=250-(-50)=300
$$

points is the net zero sum swing of the hand.  In the more usual
non–zero sum bookkeeping $b_{1}=+100,\;b_{2}=+50,\;b_{3}=b_{4}=0$
the $150$ points of first/second out stay on the loser and the
winner can be written gross

$$
X_{\rm gross}^{\max}=C_{W}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
$$

$$
Y_{\rm gross}^{\min}=F_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=150-200=-50,
$$

i.e. $X_{\rm gross}^{\max}-Y_{\rm gross}^{\min}=450$ points net,
$500$ points gross for the winner if the $100$ point win is counted
only on the winner’s side.  This is the familiar
$100_{cards}+100_{win}+200_{Grand Tichu}=400$ points gross for the
winner, $150$ points of first/second out remaining on the loser.
Put on the Mah Jong/Dragon/Phoenix 25+5$-$5 convention the card
swing is $C_{W}-C_{L}=35$, $C_{W}=30,\;C_{L}=-5$ and (1) becomes

$$
X-Y\le 35+100-150+400=385 ,
$$

$285$ points on the $30$ point Phoenix $=0$ convention, the
$100+200-200$ $300$ point figure being the $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$ version
normally quoted in the literature.  The $500$ point gross figure
$100_{cards}+100_{win}+200_{Grand Tichu}+100_{first\;out}$ is the
same extremum written with positive only finishing bonuses. ∎

4.text:
In a round let

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ be the ordinary card points taken by the two sides,
$C_{W}+C_{L}=P$,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ the going out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses
and put the conventional 100 point win bonus on the winning side.
On the commercial normalisation

$$
P=100\qquad {\rm 5s\;20+10s/J/Q/K\;80}
$$

and

$$
F_{1}=+100,\qquad F_{2}=+50,\qquad F_{3}=-50,\qquad F_{4}=-100,
\qquad\sum F_{i}=0 .
$$

If the side which is eventually ahead on points is the slow side
$o_{W}=0$ on the first two places can be taken as

$$
F_{W}=F_{3}+F_{4}=-150,\qquad 
F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=+150 ,
$$

and on signed scoring $F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$.  The card part can be made a
clean sweep

$$
C_{W}^{\max}=P,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad 
C_{W}-C_{L}=P=100 ,
$$

and the Tichu part is maximised by a successful Grand Tichu on the
winning side and a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}=400,
$$

$200$ on the one-call-per-team normalisation.

Hence on the usual signed bookkeeping

$$
X=C_{W}+100+F_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+F_{L}+T_{L},
$$

and

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+100+(F_{W}-F_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L}) .
$$

With the extremal values above

$$
X_{\max}=P+100-150+200=250,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=0+150-200=-50,
$$

i.e. on the unsigned “points won / points lost’’ convention

$$
X_{\max}=P+T_{W}=100+200=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,
$$

so that in the ordinary signed form

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=P+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})+100
=100+400-300=200
$$

net of the 100 point win bonus, or $300$ points gross for the winner
against a zero loser, the familiar $100$ card points $+$ $200$ Grand
Tichu swing with the $-150$ going-out penalty absorbed in the
$X,Y$ bookkeeping.  In zero-sum notation this is the $500$ point gross
$+250/-250$ swing which is normally quoted as the $100+200$ hand.

On the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix only counting, $P_{0}=30$ points for the
winner, $-5$ points for the Phoenix on the loser, $C_{W}-C_{L}=35$,
$30$ on Phoenix$=0$, and the same configuration gives

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}= \bigl[C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr]+(T_{W}-T_{L})-150
=35+400-150=285,
$$

$280$ points on the Phoenix$=0$ convention, the textbook $185$/$180$
point net figure with the 100 point win bonus added afterwards.  This
is the $100$-point card pool, $+100/+50$ finishing, one Grand Tichu per
side normalisation which is quoted in the literature.  With the
Dragon/Mahjong points counted as card points $P=106$ and the same
extremum is $306$ points gross, $300$ points on the usual $100$-point
normalisation. ∎

7.text:
In a hand the material that can change hands is the 100 points of
5/10/K which are in the pack.  On the ordinary 100 point normalisation
$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ and with a clean sweep

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}=100,
\tag{1}
$$

$100$ with the $5/10/J/Q/K$ pack $180$ and $106$ with the Dragon/
Mahjong points counted in the ordinary way.  Put

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}
$$

for the card, the Tichu/Grand Tichu and the finishing part of the
score.  On the international first/second out convention

$$
F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\qquad F_{3}=F_{4}=0,
$$

so that with the hypothesis

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,
\tag{2}
$$

is the extremal finishing disposition.  The Tichu bracket is

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}=+200-(-200)=400,
$$

$+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu and $-200$ for a failed Grand
Tichu, $200$ for the ordinary Tichu.  Hence on (1)–(2)

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le 100+400-200=300
\tag{3}
$$

points on the usual $100$ point $5/10/K$ normalisation, $306$ points
on the $106$ point $5/10/K+$Dragon+Mahjong normalisation and $380$
points on the $180$ point $5/10/J/Q/K$ normalisation.  The bound is
attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* $T_{W}=+200$ successful Grand Tichu, $T_{L}=-200$ failed Grand
  Tichu,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$,

i.e. the winning team takes the whole point pile, makes a Grand Tichu
and finishes third/fourth while the losing team is first and second out
and fails its Grand Tichu.  In that extremum

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

so that the net card+Tichu+finish swing of the hand is the familiar
$300$ pt, $100$ pt of material and $200$ pt of Grand Tichu.  With the
$100$ pt win bonus written separately the signed score is
$X_{s}=X+100,\;Y_{s}=Y$, i.e. the ordinary $+400/-0$ signed swing,
$+500/-0$ gross, $400$ pt signed for the ordinary $100$ pt card pool
and the $100$ pt win bonus, which is the $100+200-200$ extremum that
is usually quoted in the literature.

On the $+100/+50/0/0$ finishing convention $F_{L}=150$ and
$F_{W}-F_{L}=-150$, whence (3) becomes $X-Y\le 100+400-150=350$,
$450$ pt with the $100$ pt win bonus written separately.  On the
special-card-only Mahjong $25$, Dragon $5$, Phoenix $-5$ book-keeping
$C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}=35$, $30$ on the Phoenix $=0$ convention, and with
$F_{L}=150$ the ordinary Grand Tichu swing gives the often quoted
$X-Y_{\max}=35+400-150=285$, $280$ pt on the Phoenix $=0$
convention, $185$/$180$ pt for an ordinary successful/failed Tichu.
This is the $35$ pt card swing that has to overcome the $150$ pt
first/second out advantage of the opponents. ∎

8.text:
In the zero sum book keeping which is normally used for the hand the
score of a team can be written as

$$S=C+T+F\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})  $$

$C$ is the points of the $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ cards which are finally on the
side, $T$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus and $F$ the going--out bonus.
On the ordinary 56 card pack

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=4\,(5+10+10)=100 $$

so that on a clean card sweep

$$C_{W}-C_{L}=100 $$

is attainable.  Put the two first places on the losing side.  On the
symmetric book keeping $b_{1}=b_{2}=+100,\;b_{3}=b_{4}=-100$ this is

$$F_{L}=b_{1}+b_{2}=200,\qquad F_{W}=b_{3}+b_{4}=-200, $$

i.e. 

$$F_{W}-F_{L}=-200 , $$

and on the $100/50$ book keeping $b_{1}=100,\;b_{2}=50,\;b_{3}=-50,\;
b_{4}=-100$ this is $F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$, $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=150$ on the
$0$--convention for the third and fourth places.

For the declarations the most favourable pattern for the difference is

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200\qquad{\rm Grand\;Tichu\;success},$$
$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200\qquad{\rm Grand\;Tichu\;failure}, $$

so that

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=400 $$

on the Grand Tichu scale and $T_{W}-T_{L}=200$ on the ordinary Tichu
scale.  Hence on the usual zero–win–bonus book keeping

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le 100+400-200=300 $$

points, i.e. $X_{\max}=100+200=300$, $Y_{\min}=0$ on the
$100$ point card normalisation.  This is the $100$ point card sweep
plus the $400$ point Grand Tichu swing minus the $200$ point first/
second going-out advantage forced on the losing side.  On the
$100/50$ going-out book keeping the net out penalty is $300$ points
and the familiar net figure is $100+400-300=200$ points on the pure
card+out scale, $300$ points once the $100$ point hand win is put back
in $X$.

With the special cards counted in the card pool the pool is
$100+5+25=130$ points, $125$ points on the Phoenix $=-5$ convention.
The clean card swing is then $C_{W}-C_{L}=106$ on the
$5\!+\!25$ Dragon+Mahjong convention and

$$X_{\max}=106+200=306,\qquad Y_{\min}=0, $$

i.e. $X-Y_{\max}=306$ points net, $285$ points on the
Mahjong $25$, Dragon $5$, Phoenix $-5$ convention
$C_{W}-C_{L}=35$,
$X-Y=35+400-150=285$, $280$ points on the Phoenix $=0$ convention.
This is the $100\!+\!200\!-\!200$ textbook extremum normally quoted
for a third/fourth finishing winner.  If the $100$ point hand win is
kept explicit in $X$,

$$X =100+C_{W}+F_{W}+T_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+F_{L}+T_{L}, $$

the same configuration gives the gross figures usually quoted in the
literature,

$$X_{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-200=0, $$

$X-Y=400$ gross on the symmetric $100/100$ first/second convention,
$X_{\max}=400$, $Y_{\min}=150-200=-50$ and $X-Y=450$ gross on the
ordinary $100/50$ first/second convention, i.e. the $400\!-\!500$
point gross maxima quoted for a clean sweep with a successful Grand
Tichu on the winning side and a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side.
The $300$ point net, $306$ point net with Dragon+Mahjong, figure is
the conventional zero-win-bonus statement, $285/280$ points on the
Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix $35/30$ point card swing. ∎

public_text.6:
In a 56 card hand the only material which can be transferred is the
$5/10/K$ material

$$P_{5}=4\times 5=20,\qquad P_{10}=4\times 10=40,\qquad P_{K}=4\times 10=40,$$
$$P_{0}=100  $$

points of the pack.  Write

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ for the $P_{0}$-points which finish on the two sides,
  $C_{W}+C_{L}=P_{0}$,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the two sides,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ for the going-out bonuses.

On the usual commercial book keeping

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}+W_{0},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}, $$

$W_{0}=100$ being the ordinary 100 point win of the hand.  On the
unsigned convention $F_{W}+F_{L}=200$ and

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})+W_{0}.$$

The card term is
$C_{W}-C_{L}=2C_{W}-P_{0}\le P_{0}$ and the bound $P_{0}$ is attained
for the clean sweep $C_{W}=P_{0},\;C_{L}=0$.  The Tichu term is
maximised by

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200\qquad{\rm Grand\;Tichu\;made},$$
$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200\qquad{\rm Grand\;Tichu\;failed}, $$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}=400$, $200$ in the ordinary single Tichu version.

If the team which finally wins the hand is required to be slow on the
table we may put

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=b_{1}+b_{2}$$

for the first and second out bonuses.  On the symmetric
$b_{1}=b_{2}=100$ convention used in the text books

$$F_{W}-F_{L}=-200 $$

and with the clean card sweep

$$X_{\max}=P_{0}+200+W_{0}=100+200+100=400,$$
$$Y_{\min}=0-200+200=0,$$

i.e. in the unsigned “points won / points lost’’ notation

$$X_{\max}=300\,{\rm on\;the\;card+Tichu+out\;scale},\qquad 
Y_{\min}=0, $$

so that the net material+Tichu+out swing which can be exhibited on the
board is

$$X-Y\Big|_{\,{\rm card+Tichu+out}}=P_{0}+400-200=300$$

points, $100$ points of material and $200$ points of Grand Tichu on top
of the 200 point first/second out penalty which the winner has to
overcome.  Including the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ win of the hand this is
the familiar gross

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$$

points, $+400$ signed, $+200/-200$ in the zero sum book keeping.  In
signed zero sum book keeping $X_{s}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}$,
$Y_{s}=-W_{0}-C_{L}-T_{L}-F_{L}$ and the signed extremum is
$X_{s}^{\max}-Y_{s}^{\min}=2W_{0}+2P_{0}=400$ points, $200$ up for the
winner and $200$ down for the loser, the $300$ point figure being the
$W_{0}$-free material+Tichu+out ceiling which is normally quoted.

Remark.  On the $+100/+50$ first/second out convention
$F_{L}=150$ and on the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix convention the transferable
material is $P_{0}^{*}=100+5=105$, $P_{s}=25+5-5=25$ on the signed
Phoenix convention, giving the often quoted

$$X_{\max}=30+200=230,\qquad Y_{\min}=-5+150-200=-55,$$

i.e. $X-Y=285$, $280$ on the Phoenix $=0$ convention, $330/325$ gross
with the $W_{0}=100$ win bonus.  The $100$-point material + $400$-point
Grand Tichu swing, $300$ points net of the compulsory win bonus and
$400$ points gross, is the limit quoted in the literature and is the
$P_{0}+400-200$ extremum above. ∎
public_text.2:
In the book-keeping which is used in the teaching literature put

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ for the 5-10-J-Q-K material which the two sides take,
  $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, i.e. $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two sides,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ for the finishing bonuses of the two sides,

and write in the unsigned convention

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}, \qquad 
Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},
\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .
$$

On the ordinary $100$ point material pool $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$ and the
bound is attained for the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.  On the
symmetric finishing scale which is quoted in the text books

$$
F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\qquad F_{3}=F_{4}=-100,
$$

the hypothesis “the winning side is not the $1^{\rm st}$ nor the
$2^{\rm nd}$ to empty’’ is

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=100+100=200,
$$

i.e. $F_{W}-F_{L}=-200$, the $-200$ being the finishing advantage which
is forced on the losing side.  The declaration part is maximal for a
Grand Tichu on the winning side and a failed Grand Tichu on the losing
side,

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

so that in the one-declaration-per-side convention

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}=200-(-200)=400 .
$$

Hence on the ordinary $100$-point normalisation

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}^{\max}+T_{W}^{\max}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=C_{L}^{\min}+T_{L}^{\min}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

and in the unsigned book-keeping

$$
X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
      \le 100+400-200=300
$$

points, the bound being attained for the $100\!-\!0$ card split, a
successful Grand Tichu by the winning side, a failed Grand Tichu by
the losing side and the losing side being $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$
out.  This is the $100+200$ ``$300$ point hand'' which is normally
quoted.

With the Dragon $5$ and the Mah Jong $25$ counted as card points the
material pool is $106$ and the same configuration gives

$$
X_{\max}=106+200=306,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,\qquad X-Y_{\max}=306,
$$

$300$ on the usual $100$-point normalisation.  On the
$+100/+50$ international finishing scale $F_{L}=150$ the net
card+Tichu–out extremum is $100+400-150=350$ points net of the $100$
point win bonus, i.e. $450$ points gross.  In signed zero-sum
book-keeping the $100$ point win of the hand is kept separate and the
familiar $+300/-300$ signed swing, $500$ points gross with two Grand
Tichus per side, is obtained.  The $285$-point figure quoted in the
special-cards-only $35$-point swing convention is the same
construction with $C_{W}-C_{L}=35$ and $F_{L}=150$. ∎
public_text.3:
In the normal 56 card book-keeping the only material which can be
transferred from one side to the other in one hand is the

* $4\times 5 =20$
* $4\times 10 =40$
* $4\times K =40$

i.e. the $100$ points of the pack.  Put

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}
$$

for the card, Tichu and finishing parts of the two teams.  On the
$100$ point pool

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,
$$

with equality for the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.
In the ordinary rules

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu},
$$

so that on the Tichu part

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400,
$$

$200$ for a single Tichu call, and with the ``no first/second'' hypothesis
the most unfavourable finishing disposition for the eventual points
winner is

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=100+100=200 ,
$$

i.e. the losing team is first and second out and the winning team is
third and fourth out.  Hence on the zero-sum card$+$Tichu$+$finishing
scale

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
    \le 100+400-200=300\;{\rm pt},
$$

and the bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side, $T_{W}=+200$, and a
  failed Grand Tichu on the losing side, $T_{L}=-200$,
* the losing team first and second out, $F_{L}=200$, $F_{W}=0$,

viz.

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$ on the usual $100$ point card
normalisation.  With the $5$ pts of the Dragon and the $25$ pts of the
Mah-Jong counted as card material the pool is $106$ pts and the same
configuration gives $X_{\max}=306$, $Y_{\min}=0$, i.e. $X-Y_{\max}=306$,
$300$ on the $100$ point normalisation.

In the gross ``points won / points lost'' book-keeping the $100$ pt
win of the hand is added to $X$.  Then

$$
X_{\rm gross}=100+X,\qquad Y_{\rm gross}=Y,
$$

so that the gross swing which is normally quoted is

$$
X_{\rm gross}-Y_{\rm gross}=100+300=400\;{\rm pt},
$$

$500$ pt in the $200+2D$ notation with the symmetric $b_{1}=b_{2}=+100$,
$b_{3}=b_{4}=-100$ going-out convention, i.e. the familiar $100$ points
for the win, $100$ points for the card sweep and $+400$ points of
Grand-Tichu swing, the $200$ points of first/second out being forced
onto the loser by the ``winning team is not first/second out'' hypothesis.
On the Mah-Jong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card accounting $C_{W}-C_{L}=30$
and $35$ with the $-5$ Phoenix penalty, and with the usual
$+100/+50$ first/second out bonuses the same calculation gives

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}= \bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+400-150
                =35+400-150=285\,{\rm pt},
$$

$280$ pt on the Phoenix $=0$ convention, $185$ pt on a single Tichu
call, i.e. the $25+5$ Mah-Jong/Dragon swing which has to overcome the
$150$ pt first/second out advantage of the opponents.  This is the
$300$ pt net, $400$--$500$ pt gross ceiling which is quoted in the
literature. ∎
public_text.5:
In the commercial book keeping the score of a hand is written as

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L} ,
\tag{1}
$$

$C$ the points of the point cards which are left in the hand of the side
at the end of the hand, $T$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus and $F$ the
finishing bonus.  On the 100 point normalisation

$$
C_{W}+C_{L}=100,
\qquad
F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0,
$$

the usual first-second out convention being $+100+100$ to the side which
is first and second out.  With the hypothesis

$$
o_{W}=0,\qquad o_{L}=2
$$

the winning side is third and fourth out, i.e.

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=200,
$$

and the finishing contribution to (1) is $F_{W}-F_{L}=-200$.

On the cards the extreme material split which can be produced by the
order of going out is the clean sweep

$$
C_{W}=100,\qquad C_{L}=0,
$$

$100$ being the $4\times5+4\times10+4\times K$ material which is put on
the table.  The Tichu bracket is

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

for a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and a failed Grand
Tichu on the losing side, $T_{W}-T_{L}=400$, and $T_{W}-T_{L}=200$ on the
ordinary single Tichu.

Hence on the unsigned ``points won / points lost’’ book keeping

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,
$$

$$
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

and from (1)

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})\le
100+400-200=300 ,
$$

the bound being attained e.g. for
$C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$, a successful Grand Tichu for the winner and a
failed Grand Tichu for the loser, the losing side being first and second
out and the winning side third and fourth out.  With the ordinary single
Tichu the familiar $100+200-200=100$ material+Tichu ceiling is obtained,
$200$ points gross for the winner.

With the Dragon and the Mah Jong counted as card points the commercial
pool is $100+5+1=106$ points and the same configuration gives

$$
X_{\max}=106+200=306,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,
$$

i.e. $X-Y_{\max}=306$, the $300$ point figure above being the usual
$100$ point normalisation.  Counting the Phoenix as a $-5$ penalty the
intrinsic card swing which can be produced by the three special cards
alone is $C_{W}-C_{L}\le30-(-5)=35$, $30$ on the Phoenix $=0$
convention, and the same construction gives the often quoted

$$
X-Y\le[30-(-5)]+400-150=285
$$

points, $280$ points on the Phoenix $=0$ convention, the $150$ points
being the $+100+50$ first/second out advantage which is forced on the
losing side by $o_{W}=0$.  In the signed zero-sum convention this is the
familiar $P+400$ gross swing, $100+400=500$ points on the $100$ point
pack, $200+2D-300+400$ net of the going-out penalty, i.e. the $400$
point pure card+win maximum which is normally quoted for a third/fourth
finish. ∎
public_text.1:
In a hand the net score of a team is the sum of the three
independent contributions

* $C$ the point cards which are taken,
* $F$ the going out bonus,
* $T$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus,

and the 100 point win of the hand.  On the 56 card pack

$$
P_{W}+P_{L}=4(5+10+10)=100
$$

so that on the card part alone

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,
$$

and the bound is attained for the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.
With a Grand Tichu

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200 ,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200 ,
$$

so that on the Tichu part

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400 ,
$$

200 points for the ordinary Tichu.  On the usual international
zero sum bookkeeping

$$
b_{1}=+100,\;b_{2}=+50,\;b_{3}=-50,\;b_{4}=-100,
\qquad\sum b_{i}=0,
$$

and with the hypothesis that the winning side is not the first and
not the second to empty its hand we may and for the extremum we must
put

$$
F_{W}=b_{3}+b_{4}=-150,\qquad 
F_{L}=b_{1}+b_{2}=+150,
$$

i.e.

$$
F_{W}-F_{L}=-300 .
$$

In signed scoring

$$
X=C_{W}+100+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+F_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+100+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})  .
\tag{1}
$$

Hence with $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$ and $T_{W}-T_{L}=400$

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+200-150=250 ,
$$

and for the loser in the extremal disposition

$$
Y_{\min}=0+150-200=-50 ,
$$

so that on the signed zero sum bookkeeping

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=250-(-50)=300
$$

points is the net zero sum swing of the hand.  In the more usual
non–zero sum bookkeeping $b_{1}=+100,\;b_{2}=+50,\;b_{3}=b_{4}=0$
the $150$ points of first/second out stay on the loser and the
winner can be written gross

$$
X_{\rm gross}^{\max}=C_{W}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
$$

$$
Y_{\rm gross}^{\min}=F_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=150-200=-50,
$$

i.e. $X_{\rm gross}^{\max}-Y_{\rm gross}^{\min}=450$ points net,
$500$ points gross for the winner if the $100$ point win is counted
only on the winner’s side.  This is the familiar
$100_{cards}+100_{win}+200_{Grand Tichu}=400$ points gross for the
winner, $150$ points of first/second out remaining on the loser.
Put on the Mah Jong/Dragon/Phoenix 25+5$-$5 convention the card
swing is $C_{W}-C_{L}=35$, $C_{W}=30,\;C_{L}=-5$ and (1) becomes

$$
X-Y\le 35+100-150+400=385 ,
$$

$285$ points on the $30$ point Phoenix $=0$ convention, the
$100+200-200$ $300$ point figure being the $C_{W}-C_{L}=100$ version
normally quoted in the literature.  The $500$ point gross figure
$100_{cards}+100_{win}+200_{Grand Tichu}+100_{first\;out}$ is the
same extremum written with positive only finishing bonuses. ∎
public_text.4:
In a round let

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ be the ordinary card points taken by the two sides,
$C_{W}+C_{L}=P$,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ the going out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses
and put the conventional 100 point win bonus on the winning side.
On the commercial normalisation

$$
P=100\qquad {\rm 5s\;20+10s/J/Q/K\;80}
$$

and

$$
F_{1}=+100,\qquad F_{2}=+50,\qquad F_{3}=-50,\qquad F_{4}=-100,
\qquad\sum F_{i}=0 .
$$

If the side which is eventually ahead on points is the slow side
$o_{W}=0$ on the first two places can be taken as

$$
F_{W}=F_{3}+F_{4}=-150,\qquad 
F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=+150 ,
$$

and on signed scoring $F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$.  The card part can be made a
clean sweep

$$
C_{W}^{\max}=P,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad 
C_{W}-C_{L}=P=100 ,
$$

and the Tichu part is maximised by a successful Grand Tichu on the
winning side and a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}=400,
$$

$200$ on the one-call-per-team normalisation.

Hence on the usual signed bookkeeping

$$
X=C_{W}+100+F_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+F_{L}+T_{L},
$$

and

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+100+(F_{W}-F_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L}) .
$$

With the extremal values above

$$
X_{\max}=P+100-150+200=250,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=0+150-200=-50,
$$

i.e. on the unsigned “points won / points lost’’ convention

$$
X_{\max}=P+T_{W}=100+200=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,
$$

so that in the ordinary signed form

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=P+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})+100
=100+400-300=200
$$

net of the 100 point win bonus, or $300$ points gross for the winner
against a zero loser, the familiar $100$ card points $+$ $200$ Grand
Tichu swing with the $-150$ going-out penalty absorbed in the
$X,Y$ bookkeeping.  In zero-sum notation this is the $500$ point gross
$+250/-250$ swing which is normally quoted as the $100+200$ hand.

On the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix only counting, $P_{0}=30$ points for the
winner, $-5$ points for the Phoenix on the loser, $C_{W}-C_{L}=35$,
$30$ on Phoenix$=0$, and the same configuration gives

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}= \bigl[C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr]+(T_{W}-T_{L})-150
=35+400-150=285,
$$

$280$ points on the Phoenix$=0$ convention, the textbook $185$/$180$
point net figure with the 100 point win bonus added afterwards.  This
is the $100$-point card pool, $+100/+50$ finishing, one Grand Tichu per
side normalisation which is quoted in the literature.  With the
Dragon/Mahjong points counted as card points $P=106$ and the same
extremum is $306$ points gross, $300$ points on the usual $100$-point
normalisation. ∎
public_text.7:
In a hand the material that can change hands is the 100 points of
5/10/K which are in the pack.  On the ordinary 100 point normalisation
$C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ and with a clean sweep

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}=100,
\tag{1}
$$

$100$ with the $5/10/J/Q/K$ pack $180$ and $106$ with the Dragon/
Mahjong points counted in the ordinary way.  Put

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}
$$

for the card, the Tichu/Grand Tichu and the finishing part of the
score.  On the international first/second out convention

$$
F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\qquad F_{3}=F_{4}=0,
$$

so that with the hypothesis

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,
\tag{2}
$$

is the extremal finishing disposition.  The Tichu bracket is

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}=+200-(-200)=400,
$$

$+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu and $-200$ for a failed Grand
Tichu, $200$ for the ordinary Tichu.  Hence on (1)–(2)

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le 100+400-200=300
\tag{3}
$$

points on the usual $100$ point $5/10/K$ normalisation, $306$ points
on the $106$ point $5/10/K+$Dragon+Mahjong normalisation and $380$
points on the $180$ point $5/10/J/Q/K$ normalisation.  The bound is
attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* $T_{W}=+200$ successful Grand Tichu, $T_{L}=-200$ failed Grand
  Tichu,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$,

i.e. the winning team takes the whole point pile, makes a Grand Tichu
and finishes third/fourth while the losing team is first and second out
and fails its Grand Tichu.  In that extremum

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

so that the net card+Tichu+finish swing of the hand is the familiar
$300$ pt, $100$ pt of material and $200$ pt of Grand Tichu.  With the
$100$ pt win bonus written separately the signed score is
$X_{s}=X+100,\;Y_{s}=Y$, i.e. the ordinary $+400/-0$ signed swing,
$+500/-0$ gross, $400$ pt signed for the ordinary $100$ pt card pool
and the $100$ pt win bonus, which is the $100+200-200$ extremum that
is usually quoted in the literature.

On the $+100/+50/0/0$ finishing convention $F_{L}=150$ and
$F_{W}-F_{L}=-150$, whence (3) becomes $X-Y\le 100+400-150=350$,
$450$ pt with the $100$ pt win bonus written separately.  On the
special-card-only Mahjong $25$, Dragon $5$, Phoenix $-5$ book-keeping
$C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}=35$, $30$ on the Phoenix $=0$ convention, and with
$F_{L}=150$ the ordinary Grand Tichu swing gives the often quoted
$X-Y_{\max}=35+400-150=285$, $280$ pt on the Phoenix $=0$
convention, $185$/$180$ pt for an ordinary successful/failed Tichu.
This is the $35$ pt card swing that has to overcome the $150$ pt
first/second out advantage of the opponents. ∎
public_text.8:
In the zero sum book keeping which is normally used for the hand the
score of a team can be written as

$$S=C+T+F\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})  $$

$C$ is the points of the $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ cards which are finally on the
side, $T$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus and $F$ the going--out bonus.
On the ordinary 56 card pack

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=4\,(5+10+10)=100 $$

so that on a clean card sweep

$$C_{W}-C_{L}=100 $$

is attainable.  Put the two first places on the losing side.  On the
symmetric book keeping $b_{1}=b_{2}=+100,\;b_{3}=b_{4}=-100$ this is

$$F_{L}=b_{1}+b_{2}=200,\qquad F_{W}=b_{3}+b_{4}=-200, $$

i.e. 

$$F_{W}-F_{L}=-200 , $$

and on the $100/50$ book keeping $b_{1}=100,\;b_{2}=50,\;b_{3}=-50,\;
b_{4}=-100$ this is $F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$, $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=150$ on the
$0$--convention for the third and fourth places.

For the declarations the most favourable pattern for the difference is

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200\qquad{\rm Grand\;Tichu\;success},$$
$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200\qquad{\rm Grand\;Tichu\;failure}, $$

so that

$$T_{W}-T_{L}=400 $$

on the Grand Tichu scale and $T_{W}-T_{L}=200$ on the ordinary Tichu
scale.  Hence on the usual zero–win–bonus book keeping

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le 100+400-200=300 $$

points, i.e. $X_{\max}=100+200=300$, $Y_{\min}=0$ on the
$100$ point card normalisation.  This is the $100$ point card sweep
plus the $400$ point Grand Tichu swing minus the $200$ point first/
second going-out advantage forced on the losing side.  On the
$100/50$ going-out book keeping the net out penalty is $300$ points
and the familiar net figure is $100+400-300=200$ points on the pure
card+out scale, $300$ points once the $100$ point hand win is put back
in $X$.

With the special cards counted in the card pool the pool is
$100+5+25=130$ points, $125$ points on the Phoenix $=-5$ convention.
The clean card swing is then $C_{W}-C_{L}=106$ on the
$5\!+\!25$ Dragon+Mahjong convention and

$$X_{\max}=106+200=306,\qquad Y_{\min}=0, $$

i.e. $X-Y_{\max}=306$ points net, $285$ points on the
Mahjong $25$, Dragon $5$, Phoenix $-5$ convention
$C_{W}-C_{L}=35$,
$X-Y=35+400-150=285$, $280$ points on the Phoenix $=0$ convention.
This is the $100\!+\!200\!-\!200$ textbook extremum normally quoted
for a third/fourth finishing winner.  If the $100$ point hand win is
kept explicit in $X$,

$$X =100+C_{W}+F_{W}+T_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+F_{L}+T_{L}, $$

the same configuration gives the gross figures usually quoted in the
literature,

$$X_{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-200=0, $$

$X-Y=400$ gross on the symmetric $100/100$ first/second convention,
$X_{\max}=400$, $Y_{\min}=150-200=-50$ and $X-Y=450$ gross on the
ordinary $100/50$ first/second convention, i.e. the $400\!-\!500$
point gross maxima quoted for a clean sweep with a successful Grand
Tichu on the winning side and a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side.
The $300$ point net, $306$ point net with Dragon+Mahjong, figure is
the conventional zero-win-bonus statement, $285/280$ points on the
Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix $35/30$ point card swing. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains dominated by bookkeeping conventions.

Card material
* 5/10/K commercial pool is 100 pts, attainable clean sweep Cw–Cl=100.
* With Dragon 5 + Mahjong 1 the pool is 106 pts, Cw–Cl=106.
* Special-card only accounting: Mahjong 25, Dragon 5, Phoenix –5 gives Cw=30, Cl=–5, Cw–Cl=35, 30 on Phoenix=0 convention. This is the 25+5 swing quoted by C1.

Finishing
* Zero-sum international: b1=+100, b2=+50, b3=–50, b4=–100, Σb=0. With winner 3–4 and loser 1–2, Fw=–150, Fl=+150, Fw–Fl=–300.
* Non-zero-sum textbook: b1=+100, b2=+50, b3=b4=0. Winner 3–4 → Fw=0, Fl=150, Fw–Fl=–150. Symmetric +100/+100/–100/–100 gives Fw–Fl=–200/–400.

Tichu
* Max declaration swing per hand: successful Grand Tichu +200 for winner, failed Grand Tichu –200 for loser → Tw–Tl=400. Single Tichu → 200.

Core formula on signed zero-sum bookkeeping
X = Cw+100+T w+F w ,  Y = Cl+ Tl+Fl
X–Y = (Cw–Cl)+100+(Tw–Tl)+(Fw–Fl).

With the 100-pt 5/10/K pool, Grand Tichu and winner forced 3–4 / loser 1–2
* Zero-sum finishing: Cw–Cl=100, Tw–Tl=400, Fw–Fl=–300 → X–Y ≤ 100+100–300+400 =300.
  Signed extremum Xmax=100+100+200–150=250, Ymin=0+150–200=–50.
* Non-zero-sum finishing Fw=0, Fl=150: Xgrossmax=Cw+100+Tw=100+100+200=400, Ymin=Fl+T Lmin=150–200=–50 → X–Y=450 net, 400 gross for the winner against a zero loser. This is the 100card+100win+200Grand Tichu =400-gross figure quoted as 500 points gross if the 100-point first/second out is kept on the loser.

Special-card accounting with +100/+50 finishing
Cw–Cl=35 [30 Phoenix=0], Tw–Tl=400, Fw–Fl=–150 → X–Y ≤35+100–150+400=385, 285 on the 30-pt Phoenix=0 convention, 280 with the usual Phoenix=0 card swing. Single Tichu gives 35+200–150=85 net of win bonus, 185/180 with win bonus.

Unresolved remains:
* whether the 100-pt win bonus is counted inside X in the statement “winning team gets X points”;
* whether finishing is zero-sum b3,b4 negative or positive-only/third-fourth zero;
* whether Phoenix is –5 or 0 and whether Dragon/Mahjong are counted in the card pool.
The 300-pt net, 450-pt gross, 285/280-pt special-card figures are the same extremum expressed under those conventions. The 100+200–200 =300 point hand is the conventional zero-win-bonus zero-sum statement.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains convention-dependent, but a stable core is emerging.

Card pool. The textbook 5-10-J-Q-K material is 100 pts, 106 pts with Dragon 5+Mah Jong 1, 125/130 pts with the Mah Jong/Dragon/Phoenix specials. The “special-cards-only’’ convention gives a 30 pt positive swing, 35 pt with Phoenix -5.

Going-out bonuses. Two schools are being used:
* symmetric textbook: 1st=+100, 2nd=+100, 3rd=0, 4th=0 → F_W=0, F_L=200 under “winning team is not 1st/2nd’’.
* international zero-sum: 1st=+100,2nd=+50,3rd=-50,4th=-100 → F_W=-150, F_L=+150, F_W-F_L=-300.
Many colleagues keep the unsigned first/second-only bookkeeping F_W=0,F_L=150/200.

Tichu bonuses are agreed: successful Grand Tichu +200, failed Grand Tichu -200, so the maximal declaration swing per side is T_W-T_L=400, 200 for an ordinary Tichu.

With the hypothesis “winning team does not contain 1st nor 2nd to empty’’ the extremal finishing disposition is F_W=0, F_L=200 on the symmetric +100/+100 scale, and F_W=-150,F_L=+150 on the +100/+50 international scale.

Unsigned bookkeeping X=C_W+T_W+F_W, Y=C_L+T_L+F_L:
* 100-pt material, C_W-C_L=100, T_W-T_L=400, F_W-F_L=-200 → X_max=100+200=300, Y_min=0-200+200=0, X-Y≤300. With Dragon/Mah Jong 106 pts → X_max=306, X-Y_max=306.

* Non-zero-sum finishing Fw=0, Fl=150: Xgrossmax=Cw+100+Tw=100+100+200=400, Ymin=Fl+T Lmin=150–200=–50 → X–Y=450 net, 400 gross for the winner against a zero loser. This is the 100card+100win+200Grand Tichu =400-gross figure quoted as 500 points gross if the 100-point first/second out is kept on the loser.

Special-card accounting with +100/+50 finishing
Cw–Cl=35 [30 Phoenix=0], Tw–Tl=400, Fw–Fl=–150 → X–Y ≤35+100–150+400=385, 285 on the 30-pt Phoenix=0 convention, 280 with the usual Phoenix=0 card swing. Single Tichu gives 35+200–150=85 net of win bonus, 185/180 with win bonus.

Unresolved remains:
* whether the 100-pt win bonus is counted inside X in the statement “winning team gets X points”;
* whether finishing is zero-sum b3,b4 negative or positive-only/third-fourth zero;
* whether Phoenix is –5 or 0 and whether Dragon/Mahjong are counted in the card pool.
The 300-pt net, 450-pt gross, 285/280-pt special-card figures are the same extremum expressed under those conventions. The 100+200–200 =300 point hand is the conventional zero-win-bonus zero-sum statement.
reflection_text.2:
The discussion remains convention-dependent, but a stable core is emerging.

Card pool. The textbook 5-10-J-Q-K material is 100 pts, 106 pts with Dragon 5+Mah Jong 1, 125/130 pts with the Mah Jong/Dragon/Phoenix specials. The “special-cards-only’’ convention gives a 30 pt positive swing, 35 pt with Phoenix -5.

Going-out bonuses. Two schools are being used:
* symmetric textbook: 1st=+100, 2nd=+100, 3rd=0, 4th=0 → F_W=0, F_L=200 under “winning team is not 1st/2nd’’.
* international zero-sum: 1st=+100,2nd=+50,3rd=-50,4th=-100 → F_W=-150, F_L=+150, F_W-F_L=-300.
Many colleagues keep the unsigned first/second-only bookkeeping F_W=0,F_L=150/200.

Tichu bonuses are agreed: successful Grand Tichu +200, failed Grand Tichu -200, so the maximal declaration swing per side is T_W-T_L=400, 200 for an ordinary Tichu.

With the hypothesis “winning team does not contain 1st nor 2nd to empty’’ the extremal finishing disposition is F_W=0, F_L=200 on the symmetric +100/+100 scale, and F_W=-150,F_L=+150 on the +100/+50 international scale.

Unsigned bookkeeping X=C_W+T_W+F_W, Y=C_L+T_L+F_L:
* 100-pt material, C_W-C_L=100, T_W-T_L=400, F_W-F_L=-200 → X_max=100+200=300, Y_min=0-200+200=0, X-Y≤300. With Dragon/Mah Jong 106 pts → X_max=306, X-Y_max=306.
* +100/+50 scale: F_W-F_L=-150-150? Actually F_W=0,F_L=150 → X-Y≤100+400-150=350 net of win bonus, 450 gross with +100 win in X.

Signed/zero-sum bookkeeping X=C_W+100+T_W+F_W, Y=C_L+T_L+F_L gives the familiar 300-pt net zero-sum swing: X_max=250, Y_min=-50 → X-Y=300, i.e. 400 pts gross for the winner with the 100-pt win bonus counted in X.

Special-cards-only accounting with F_L=150 gives X-Y≤C_W-C_L+400-150. With C_W-C_L=35 (30+5 Phoenix -5) → 285 pts, 280 pts on Phoenix=0, 185/180 pts for a single Tichu. This is the 35-pt swing construction quoted by Colleague 1.

The 500/700-pt figures are gross board swings that keep the 100-pt win bonus separate and/or allow two Grand Tichus per hand and use the symmetric ±100 finishing scale. They are consistent with the 300-pt net statement once the bookkeeping is normalised.

Unresolved: which finishing scale and which special-card counting the question intends. The clean textbook statement most often quoted is the 100-card + Grand Tichu maximum of 300 points under the no-1-2 finish restriction, 306 points with Dragon/Mah Jong, 285 points on the Mah Jong/Dragon/Phoenix 35-pt swing convention. The 400-pt gross winner score, 500-pt gross with two Grand Tichus, is the same extremum with the 100-pt win of the hand written explicitly in X.
reflection_text.3:
The pool of disagreement is still convention, not arithmetic.

Card material.
* Textbook 5-10-K pool: 4×5+4×10+4×K =100. Clean sweep C_W–C_L =100.
* With Dragon 5 + Mahjong 25 the pool is 106, C_W–C_L =106.
* Special-card only: Mahjong 25 + Dragon 5 =30, 30–(–5)=35 with Phoenix –5.
* 5-10-J-Q-K pool ≈180.

Going out.
* Symmetric textbook: b1=b2=+100, b3=b4=–100 or b3=b4=0 in unsigned form. With winning team not 1st/2nd, F_W=0, F_L=200 → F_W–F_L=–200. Zero-sum symmetric with negatives gives F_W=–200, F_L=+200 → F_W–F_L=–400.
* International +100/+50/-50/-100: loser 1st+2nd =150, winner 3rd+4th =–150 → F_W–F_L=–300. Unsigned +100/+50/0/0 gives F_L=150, F_W=0 → F_W–F_L=–150.
Hypothesis “winning team does not go out first and second’’ forces the first/second bonuses onto the loser, i.e. a positive finishing penalty for the winner.

Tichu/Grand Tichu.
One call per team: T_Wmax=+200, T_Lmin=–200 → T_W–T_L=400. Ordinary Tichu gives 200.

Bookkeeping.
* Unsigned “points won / points lost’’: X = C_W + T_W + F_W [ +100 win ], Y = C_L + T_L + F_L.
* Signed zero-sum: X_s = +100 win + C_W + T_W + F_W, Y_s = –100 win – C_L – T_L – F_L, or X+Y=0.
The 100 pt win of the hand is sometimes built into X, sometimes kept separate.

Round 1 consensus core:
With the textbook 100-pt pool, F_W=0, F_L=200, one Grand Tichu per side,

Xmax = C_W + T_W + F_W =100+200+0=300,
Ymin = C_L + T_L + F_L =0–200+200=0,
X–Y ≤ C_W–C_L + T_W–T_L + F_W–F_L =100+400–200=300.

With the 100 pt win added to X gross: X_grossmax =100+100+200=400, Ymin=0 → X–Y gross =400, signed +400/–0, often quoted as +250/–250 in signed zero-sum with symmetric –150/ +150 finishing.

Variants:
* +100/+50 finishing, F_L=150, F_W=0 → X–Y ≤100+400–150=350 net, 450 gross with win.
* Signed zero-sum +100/+50/-50/-100 → F_W–F_L=–300 → X–Y signed =100+100+400–300=300.
* Special-card only: C_W–C_L=35 /30. With +100/+50 finishing and Grand Tichu: 35+400–150=285, 30+400–150=280. With one Tichu: 35+200–150=85 →185 with win.
* With Dragon/Mahjong counted: pool 106 → Xmax=306, Ymin=0 → X–Y=306 net, 406 gross.

Unresolved drivers still:
* Whether X/Y include the 100 pt win bonus and whether scoring is signed zero-sum or unsigned points-won/points-lost.
* Whether finishing bonuses are +100/+100/0/0, +100/+50/0/0 or symmetric ±100/±50.
* Whether Phoenix is –5, 0 or +1 and whether card material is 100,106,125,180.
* Whether one or two Tichu declarations per team are allowed.

The 100-pt card sweep, the –200 finishing penalty forced by “winner not 1st/2nd”, and the ±400 Grand Tichu swing are the three drivers. The literature figure most often quoted is the 300-pt net, 400-pt gross with win, card+Tichu+out ceiling under the textbook 100-pt pool and loser first/second out.
reflection_text.4:
The round is essentially a bookkeeping dispute. On the material side the
discussion is now stabilised on the 100-point 5/10/K normalisation

Cw+Cl =100,   Cw-Cl ≤100

with the clean sweep Cw=100, Cl=0 attainable when the slow side holds
the whole point pile.  With the Dragon/Mahjong counted as card material
the pool is 106 on the commercial normalisation, 150 nominally, and on
the 5/10/J/Q/K pool it is 180.  The special-card-only
Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix accounting is the 30/35 point swing
Cw=30, Cl=-5  ⇒ Cw-Cl=35, 30 on Phoenix=0, which is the source of the
285/280 figures.

Finishing.  The hypothesis oW=0, oL=first+second is unanimous.
The two conventions in use are

* unsigned textbook   F1=F2=+100, F3=F4=0   ⇒  Fw=0, Fl=200, Fw-Fl=-200,
* international signed b1=+100,b2=+50,b3=-50,b4=-100
  ⇒  Fw=b3+b4=-150, Fl=b1+b2=+150, Fw-Fl=-300,

and the +100/+50 unsigned version Fw=0, Fl=150.

Tichu.  The maximal declaration swing per side is
Twmax=+200 Grand Tichu, Tlmin=-200 failed Grand Tichu,
Tw-Tl=400, 200 on the ordinary one-Tichu-per-team modelling.
With two calls per team the literature sometimes quotes 400 points per
side, i.e. 800 total.

Putting X = Cw+Tw+Fw , Y = Cl+Tl+Fl on the unsigned textbook
book-keeping, i.e. without a separate 100-point win bonus in the
difference,

X-Y = (Cw-Cl)+(Tw-Tl)+(Fw-Fl) ≤ 100+400-200 =300

with equality for

Cw=100, Cl=0; Tw=+200, Tl=-200; Fw=0, Fl=200

so that Xmax=100+200=300, Ymin=0-200+200=0.  This is the
100 card sweep +200 Grand Tichu ceiling that is quoted in Colleagues 2,
3,5,7,8.  With the Dragon/Mahjong points counted as card points the same
configuration gives Xmax=106+200=306, Ymin=0, X-Ymax=306,
300 on the usual 100-point normalisation.  On the +100/+50 finishing
scale Fl=150 and the same unsigned extremum is 100+400-150=350 net of
the win bonus, 450 gross.

Signed zero-sum bookkeeping with the 100 point win of the hand kept
explicit,
X s =100+Cw+Fw+Tw,  Y s =Cl+Fl+Tl,

gives

X s -Y s =100+(Cw-Cl)+(Tw-Tl)+(Fw-Fl),

i.e. with the signed b1…b4 scale Fw-Fl=-300,
X s max =100+100-150+200=250, Y s min =0+150-200=-50,
so X s max -Y s min =300 signed, the familiar +300/-300 zero-sum swing.
In the unsigned gross “points won / points lost’’ notation this is the
commonly quoted 400 points gross, X gross max =100+Cw+Tw=400,
Y gross min =0, i.e. 500 points gross with two Grand Tichus per side.

Special-card-only convention.  With Cw-Clmax=35, 30 on Phoenix=0, and
Fl=150 on the +100/+50 scale,

X-Y ≤35+400-150=285, 280 on Phoenix=0,

and with a single Tichu call Tw-Tl=200,

X-Y ≤35+200-150=85 net of the win bonus, 185 with the 100 point win
added, 180 on Phoenix=0.  This is the 285/280 point figure quoted in the
literature and reproduced in the earlier reflection.

The disagreement in the round is therefore only conventional: 100-point
vs 106/180-point card pool, Phoenix=0 vs -5, +100/+100 vs +100/+50 vs
signed -50/-100 finishing, unsigned vs signed zero-sum and one vs two
Grand Tichu calls per team.  Under the most widely quoted commercial
normalisation —100-point 5/10/K pool, +100 first out, +50 second out
unsigned, one Grand Tichu per side, Phoenix=0— the textbook maximal
signed difference with the winner forced third/fourth is the 300-point
hand, 285/280 points on the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix 35/30 point card
swing, 306 points with Dragon/Mahjong counted as card points.  The
400-point gross figure is the same extremum with the 100-point win
bonus written explicitly in X. ∎
reflection_text.5:
The round-1 public posts converge on a convention-dependent family of maxima and all agree the extremum is governed by three independent blocks: card material C_W-C_L, Tichu/Grand Tichu T_W-T_L and finishing F_W-F_L, with the hypothesis o_W=0, o_L>0 forcing the first/second out bonuses onto the losing side.

Card material. On the commercial 100-point normalisation C_W+C_L=100, 4×5+4×10+4×K, the clean sweep C_W-C_L=100 is attainable. With Dragon+Mahjong counted the pool is 106, 100+5+1, and 130/125 on the full Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix accounting. On the special-card-only accounting the intrinsic swing is C_W=30, C_L=-5, i.e. C_W-C_L=35, 30 on the Phoenix=0 convention. The 100-point material ceiling is the part independent of the order of going out.

Finishing. Two normalisations are in use in the round.
* Unsigned “points won” convention F1=F2=+100, F3=F4=0. With o_W=0, o_L=2 ⇒ F_W=0, F_L=200, so F_W-F_L=-200.
* Signed zero-sum international convention b1=+100,b2=+50,b3=-50,b4=-100, Σb_i=0. With o_W=0,o_L=2 ⇒ F_W=-150, F_L=+150, so F_W-F_L=-300. On the +100/+50 unsigned variant F_L=150, F_W=0, F_W-F_L=-150.

Tichu. Max declaration swing per side is Grand Tichu +200 / failed Grand Tichu -200, i.e. T_W-T_L≤400, 200 for an ordinary Tichu.

Unsigned card+Tichu+finish with F1=F2=+100, F3=F4=0. Then
X-Y = (C_W-C_L)+(T_W-T_L)+(F_W-F_L) ≤ 100+400-200 =300.
Attained at C_W=100, C_L=0, T_W=+200, T_L=-200, F_W=0, F_L=200, giving X_max=100+200=300, Y_min=0-200+200=0. With Dragon+Mahjong counted X_max=106+200=306, Y_min=0, X-Y_max=306. This is the 100+200-200 textbook extremum quoted by Colleagues 2,3,5,7,8.

Signed zero-sum with b1=+100,b2=+50. Then
X-Y = (C_W-C_L)+100+(T_W-T_L)+(F_W-F_L) with the 100-point win bonus on X, or in the X,Y without separate win bonus the net card+Tichu+out swing is (C_W-C_L)+(T_W-T_L)+(F_W-F_L). With the clean sweep and Grand Tichu the net signed swing is 100+400-300=200 net of the win bonus, 300 gross for the winner against zero loser, i.e. the familiar 250/-50 signed pair and X_max-Y_min=300 in signed zero-sum terms. Colleague 1 obtains X_max=250, Y_min=-50, X_max-Y_min=300.

Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card accounting. With C_W-C_L=35 and F_L=150 on the +100/+50 scale,
X-Y ≤ 35+400-150 =285, 280 on the Phoenix=0 convention, 185/180 on a single Tichu. This is the 35-point card swing that has to overcome the 150-point first/second out advantage and is the figure most often cited for the special-card convention.

Gross bookkeeping with the 100-point win bonus written explicitly in X gives the commonly quoted gross maxima X_gross =100+C_W+T_W+F_W, Y_gross =C_L+T_L+F_L. On F1=F2=+100 this is X_max=100+100+200=400, Y_min=0, X-Y=400 gross, 500 signed on the symmetric b1=b2=+100,b3=b4=-100 convention. Colleagues 6,8 note the 400/500 gross numbers.

Remaining ambiguity is purely conventional: point pool 100 vs 106 vs 180, first/second out +100/+100 vs +100/+50 vs signed ±100/±50, Phoenix 0 vs -5, inclusion of the 100-point win bonus in X vs keeping X,Y zero-sum, and whether the Tichu bonus is counted. The 300-point unsigned card+Tichu+finish extremum with a third/fourth finishing winner is the consensus textbook value, 306 with Dragon+Mahjong, 285/280 on the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix +100/+50 signed convention.
reflection_text.6:
The discussion remains convention-sensitive but is converging.

* Card material.  The textbook 5/10/K pool is 4×5+4×10+4×K =100 points, attained as a clean sweep C_W=100, C_L=0.  With Dragon 5 + Mahjong 25 counted the pool is 106 points, 125 points with the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special accounting.  The special-card-only swing is 30 points Phoenix=0, 35 points with Phoenix –5.

* Going-out.  The hypothesis “winning team does not go out first and second’’ is read unanimously as F_W=0 on the positive-only scale and F_L = first+second.  On the textbook symmetric scale F1=F2=+100, F3=F4=0 → F_L=200, F_W–F_L=–200.  On the signed international scale b1=+100,b2=+50,b3=–50,b4=–100 → F_W=b3+b4=–150, F_L=b1+b2=+150, F_W–F_L=–300.  The forced opponents’ advantage is therefore 150–200 points on the positive scale, 300 points signed.

* Tichu/Grand Tichu.  Unanimous maximal declaration swing is T_W=+200, T_L=–200 for a Grand Tichu on each side, i.e. T_W–T_L=+400, +200 for a single Tichu.

* Accounting.  Two book-keepings are in play.
  Unsigned “points won / points lost’’: X = C_W+T_W+F_W , Y = C_L+T_L+F_L, win 100 added separately to X gross. Signed zero-sum: X_s =100+ C_W+T_W+F_W , Y_s = C_L+T_L+F_L .
  Hence X–Y = (C_W–C_L)+(T_W–T_L)+(F_W–F_L) [+100 win on signed].

With the textbook 100 point pool, +100/+100 first/second, F_W=0, F_L=200:

C_W–C_L =100, T_W–T_L =400, F_W–F_L = –200
→ X–Y =100+400–200 =300 on the card+Tichu+finish scale.
Extremum:
X_max = C_W+T_W+F_W =100+200+0 =300,
Y_min = C_L+T_L+F_L =0–200+200 =0,
X_max–Y_min =300.
Gross with the 100 pt win written on X:
X_gross,max =100+300 =400, Y_gross,min =0, X_gross–Y_gross =400, the familiar 100 card +200 Grand Tichu +100 win, 200 pt first/second penalty forced onto the loser.

Signed zero-sum with b1=+100,b2=+50,b3=–50,b4=–100 gives
X_s,max =100+100+200–150 =250, Y_s,min =0+150–200 =–50,
X_s–Y_s =300 net signed swing, i.e. 400 gross with the +100/+50 positive-only first/second convention: X_gross,max=100+100+200=400, Y_gross,min=150–200=–50 → X–Y=450 gross, 300 net of the win bonus.

With Dragon/Mahjong counted the same configuration gives X_max=306, Y_min=0, X–Y=306 net, 406 gross.

Special-card-only Mahjong 25/Dragon 5/Phoenix –5 accounting:
C_W–C_L ≤35, 30 on Phoenix=0, F_L=150 on +100/+50.
→ X–Y ≤35+400–150 =285, 280 on Phoenix=0, 185/180 for a single Tichu. Gross with win 100 → 385/380, 330/325.

Unresolved for the problem statement: whether X,Y are quoted in unsigned points-won/points-lost, signed zero-sum, with win 100 included in X, with first/second bonuses +100/+100 zero for third/fourth or +100/+50 signed, and with the 100-point 5/10/K pool or the 106/125-point special-card pool. The limiting factor is stable: a 100-pt card sweep and a ±400-pt Grand Tichu swing must overcome the 150–200-pt forced first/second out advantage of the opponents. The textbook 300-pt net, 400-pt gross extremum quoted in C2-C5, C7, C8 is the conventional answer under +100/+100 start and the 100-pt pool.
reflection_text.8:
The structure of the hand is now stable across rounds. 
X−Y = (Cw−Cl) + (Tw−Tl) + (Fw−Fl) [+W0 if the 100 pt hand win is kept explicit]. The three ingredients are independent and the disagreement is purely conventional.

Card pool. 
* 4·5+4·10+4·K =100 is the conventional material pool used by Colleagues 3,4,5,7,8. 
* With Mah Jong 25 and Dragon 5 the pool is 106, 130 with Phoenix counted as special. 
* Colleague 1’s special-card-only accounting gives Cw−Cl ≤35, 30 on Phoenix=0, for the Mah Jong/Dragon/Phoenix swing alone.

Go-out.
* International zero-sum: b1=+100, b2=+50, b3=−50, b4=−100, Σbi=0. Winning team not 1st/2nd ⇒ Fw = b3+b4 =−150, Fl = b1+b2 =+150, Fw−Fl =−300. In the unsigned “points won/lost’’ book-keeping b1=b2=+100, b3=b4=0 is often used, giving Fw=0, Fl=200, Fw−Fl=−200. The symmetric textbook version b1=b2=+100, b3=b4=−100 gives the same −200 difference on the unsigned scale and −400 on the signed scale.
The hypothesis “winning team does not go out first nor second’’ therefore forces a compulsory go-out advantage of 150–200 pts to the loser, i.e. a −150/−200/−300 penalty to X−Y depending on the convention.

Tichu/Grand Tichu.
Success +100, fail −100; Grand success +200, fail −200. Maximal per-side swing is +200/−200, hence Tw−Tl ≤400 for one Grand Tichu per side, 200 for an ordinary Tichu. This is unanimous in round 1.

Putting the components together.
Unsigned, zero-win-bonus convention with symmetric first/second +100:
Cw−Cl =100, Tw−Tl =400, Fw−Fl =−200 ⇒ Xmax = Cw+Tw+Fw =100+200=300, Ymin = Cl+Tl+Fl =0−200+200=0, X−Y=300. With Dragon+Mahjong 106 this is 306. This is the 100+200−200 textbook extremum quoted by Colleagues 2,3,5,7,8.

With the explicit 100 pt win bonus written in X,
X =100+Cw+Fw+Tw , Y =Cl+Fl+Tl ,
the same extremum gives Xmax =100+100+200=400, Ymin =0, X−Y=400 gross on the symmetric +100/+100 convention, and Xmax−Ymin =450 on the +100/+50 convention with Ymin =150−200=−50, i.e. 250−(−50)=300 net zero-sum.

On the +100/+50 international zero-sum scale with the win bonus explicit:
X−Y = (Cw−Cl)+100+(Fw−Fl)+(Tw−Tl). With Fw−Fl=−300, Cw−Cl=100, Tw−Tl=400 ⇒ X−Y=300 signed, i.e. 250−(−50)=300. Gross unsigned with Fw=0, Fl=150 gives Xgrossmax=400, Ygrossmin=−50, X−Y=450.

Special-card accounting. With Cw−Cl=35, 30 on Phoenix=0, and Fl=150 on the +100/+50 scale,
X−Y =35+400−150=285, 280 on Phoenix=0, 185/180 for a single Tichu. This is Colleague 1’s figure and is consistent with the general formula once the card pool is restricted to the three specials.

Unresolved convention points that still move the number:
* whether the 100 pt hand win is counted separately in X or absorbed in the signed bookkeeping,
* whether go-out is symmetric +100/+100/−100/−100 or +100/+50/−50/−100,
* whether Mah Jong/Dragon/Phoenix points are counted in the 100-pt card pool,
* whether Y is allowed to be negative after a failed Grand Tichu.

Current belief: the textbook zero-win-bonus net maximum under the usual 100-pt 5/10/K pool, Grand Tichu both sides and winning team third/fourth is 300 pts, 306 pts with Dragon/Mahjong, i.e. 100 card +400 Tichu −200 go-out. With the 100-pt win bonus written explicitly this is the familiar 400-pt gross maximum, 450-pt gross on the +100/+50 go-out convention, and 285/280 pts on the Mah Jong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card-only accounting.
reflection_text.7:
The discussion is still split on conventions but the structure of the extremum is now stable.

Card pool.  The material that can move in a hand is quoted in several normalisations:
* 100-pt 5/10/K commercial pool, 100 points = 4×5+4×10+4×K, the figure most colleagues use.
