On the unsigned points-won/points-lost book keeping X = C_W+T_W+F_W, Y = C_L+T_L+F_L, with the 100-pt win bonus often written separately as X_gross = X+100.

* 100-pt pool, symmetric +100/+100 finish, Grand Tichu:
  C_W–C_L =100, T_W–T_L =400, F_W–F_L = –200.
  X_max =100+200=300, Y_min =0–200+200=0, X–Y =300, the 100+200 extremum that is now quoted by Colleagues 2,3,5,7,8. Gross with the 100-pt win written in X is X_gross_max =400, X_gross–Y =400. With Dragon+Mahjong the pool is 106 and the same configuration gives 306/0, i.e. 306 net, 406 gross.

* +100/+50 finish, zero-sum book keeping:
  F_W = –150, F_L = +150, F_W–F_L = –300. Signed scoring X = C_W+100+T_W+F_W, Y = C_L+T_L+F_L gives X_max =250, Y_min = –50 and signed X–Y =300, the 300-pt signed swing often cited. Gross unsigned with F_W=0,F_L=150 gives X_max =400, Y_min = –50, X–Y≈450, i.e. 350 net of win bonus.

* Special-cards-only convention.
  C_W–C_L max =35, 30 on Phoenix=0. With +100/+50 finish and Grand Tichu:
  X–Y =35+400–150 =285, 280 on Phoenix=0, 185/180 for a single Tichu. This is the 285/280 figure repeatedly given by Colleague 1.

Unresolved. The problem setter’s intended normalisation is not settled: 100-pt 5/10/K vs 106-pt with Dragon/Mahjong vs 35-pt special-card pool, and +100/+50/0/0 vs +100/+100/0/0 vs zero-sum +100/+50/–50/–100, and whether Phoenix is –5 or 0 and whether Y is allowed to be negative. Under the most common international textbook normalisation – 100-pt card pool, +100/+100 first/second out, Grand Tichu ±200, winner 3rd/4th – the textbook net maximum is X–Y =300 points, 400 points gross including the compulsory 100-pt win bonus, 306/406 with Dragon+Mahjong counted. The 285/280 special-card version is the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix extremum. This remains the working consensus to carry forward.

6.text:
On the 56 card pack the only transferable material is the

$C_{W}+C_{L}=4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K=100$ 

$5/10/K$ points.  In the unsigned book-keeping which is used in the
text books

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}$$

is the card, Tichu and going-out part of the two teams.  On a clean
sweep

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0, $$

and on the Tichu bracket

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu},$$

so that

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400,$$

$200$ for an ordinary Tichu.

On the textbook $+100/+100/0/0$ finishing scale the hypothesis
$o_{W}=0$ is

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=100+100=200 ,$$

i.e. $F_{W}-F_{L}=-200$; the losing side is forced to be first and
second out.  Hence on the card$+$Tichu$+$finish scale

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le 100+400-200=300 $$

and the bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* $T_{W}=+200$ successful Grand Tichu, $T_{L}=-200$ failed Grand
  Tichu,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$,

the winning side being third and fourth out.  In particular

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0, $$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$ points of card$+$Tichu$+$finish is the
usual $100+200$ net swing which has to overcome the $200$ point
first/second out advantage forced on the loser.

With the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ hand win written on the winner this is
the familiar gross figure

$$X^{g}_{ \max}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad Y^{g}_{\min}=0,$$

i.e. $X^{g}-Y^{g}=400$ gross, $500$ points on the signed
$b_{1}=+100,b_{2}=+50,b_{3}=-50,b_{4}=-100$ zero–sum scale.  On the
$+100/+50$ international first/second scale $F_{L}=150$,
$F_{W}-F_{L}=-150$ and the same extremum is $100+400-150=350$ net of
the win bonus, $450$ gross with the $100$ point win, $250-(-50)=300$
signed zero–sum swing.  With the Dragon $5$ and Mah-Jong $25$ counted
as card material the pool is $106$ and the same configuration gives
$X_{\max}=306$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y_{\max}=306$, $406$ gross with the
$100$ point win.  The $285$ point, $280$ on Phoenix$=0$, figure is the
Mahjong $25$+Dragon $5$+Phoenix $-5$ special-card only version with
$F_{L}=150$. ∎

8.text:
In the ordinary $56$ card book keeping let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=P$ be the $5/10/K$ material which is taken,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ the finishing bonuses.

On the commercial $P=100$ normalisation

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}\le P ,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}=P
$$

is the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.  For one declaration per
side

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200
$$

is a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and a failed Grand
Tichu on the losing side, so that

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400 ,
$$

$200$ on the ordinary Tichu scale.

Put the $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$ places on the losing side.  On the
symmetric text book finishing scale $F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0$
the hypothesis $o_{W}\ne1,2$ is

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200 ,
$$

i.e. $F_{W}-F_{L}=-200$.  On the unsigned card+Tichu+out book
keeping

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},
$$

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .
$$

Hence on the $100$ point normalisation

$$
X-Y\le P+400-200=300\;{\rm pt}
$$

and the bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* $T_{W}=+200$ Grand Tichu made, $T_{L}=-200$ Grand Tichu failed,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$,

i.e.

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

so that the net material $+$ Tichu $+$ finishing swing of a
third/fourth finishing winner is the familiar $100+200$ hand.
With the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ point win of the hand written
separately,

$$
X_{g}=W_{0}+X,\qquad Y_{g}=Y,
$$

$$
X_{g}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad Y_{g}^{\min}=0,
$$

the $100_{{\rm win}}+100_{{\rm cards}}+200_{{\rm Grand\;Tichu}}$ gross
maximum which is normally quoted.  On the $106$ point
$5/10/K+$Dragon$+$Mah-Jong pool this is $306$ net, $406$ gross.

In signed zero-sum international book keeping
$F_{1}=+100,\;F_{2}=+50,\;F_{3}=-50,\;F_{4}=-100$ the same extremum is

$$
F_{W}=F_{3}+F_{4}=-150,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=+150,
$$

$F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$, and with the $W_{0}=100$ win kept explicit

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{0}+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le100+100+400-300=300
$$

signed, i.e. $X_{\max}=250,\;Y_{\min}=-50$ on the signed scale and
$X_{g}^{\max}-Y_{g}^{\min}=450$ points gross, $400$ points on the
symmetric $100/100$ finishing convention.  This is the $100+400-200$
text-book ceiling, $285$ points, $280$ points on the Phoenix$=0$
convention, on the Mah-Jong $25$, Dragon $5$, Phoenix $-5$ special-card
only accounting $C_{W}-C_{L}=35$. ∎

4.text:
In the signed zero sum book keeping which is used for the hand write

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ the $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ material which finishes on the two
sides $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ the going out bonus.

On the international scale

$$b_{1}=+100,\;b_{2}=+50,\;b_{3}=-50,\;b_{4}=-100,
\qquad\sum b_{i}=0 , $$

and with $o_{W}=0$ we can put the two first places on the loser

$$F_{W}=b_{3}+b_{4}=-150,\qquad 
F_{L}=b_{1}+b_{2}=+150, $$

so that $F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$.  On the material

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le C_{W}+C_{L}=100,
$$

with equality for the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.  On the
declaration part

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

Grand Tichu made and Grand Tichu failed, so that

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400,$$
$200$ on the ordinary one-Tichu-per-side convention.

On signed scoring

$$X_{s}=100+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad 
Y_{s}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}, $$

and

$$X_{s}-Y_{s}=100+(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .
\tag{1}$$

Hence in the extremal disposition

$$C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0,\qquad 
T_{W}=+200,\;T_{L}=-200,\qquad 
F_{W}=-150,\;F_{L}=+150, $$

i.e. the winner takes the whole $100$ point pile, makes a Grand Tichu,
fails the opponent's Grand Tichu and is third and fourth out while the
loser is first and second out, we obtain

$$X_{s}^{\max}=100+100+200-150=250,\qquad
Y_{s}^{\min}=0+150-200=-50, $$

and from (1)

$$X_{s}^{\max}-Y_{s}^{\min}=100+100+400-300=300 $$

points net zero sum, the familiar $+300/-300$ swing of the hand.
In the unsigned card+Tichu+finish book keeping $X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}$,
$Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}$ this is

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}=100+200=300,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+150=-50,
$$

$Y_{\min}=0$ on the $F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ unsigned
text-book convention, i.e. the ordinary $300$ point hand

$$X-Y\le(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})\le
100+400-200=300, $$

$X_{\max}=300,\;Y_{\min}=0$ on the $F_{W}=0,F_{L}=200$ textbook scale.
With the $100$ point win of the hand written explicitly in $X$ this is
the often quoted gross

$$X_{\rm gross}^{\max}=100+C_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400, $$

$Y_{\rm gross}^{\min}=0$, $X_{\rm gross}^{\max}-Y_{\rm gross}^{\min}=400$
points gross for the winner, $500$ points gross on the symmetric
$100/100$ first/second convention.

Counting the Dragon $5$ and the Mah Jong $25$ as card material the
pool is $106$ and the same extremum is $X_{\max}=306$, $X-Y_{\max}=306$,
$300$ on the usual $100$ point normalisation.  On the special-card-only
Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix convention $C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}=35$, $30$ on
Phoenix$=0$, and with $F_{L}=150$ the Grand-Tichu extremum gives the
text-book

$$X-Y\le35+400-150=285,\qquad 280\;{\rm on\;Phoenix}=0, $$

$185/180$ points for an ordinary Tichu.  This is the $100+200-200$
$300$ point net, $400$ point gross ceiling normally quoted for a
third/fourth finishing winner. ∎

3.text:
In the ordinary book keeping let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=P$ be the $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ material which is taken,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus of the two sides,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ the going-out bonus of the two sides

and write on the unsigned $ {\rm points\;won/points\;lost}$ convention

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .
$$

On the 56 card pack

$$P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100 $$

and the clean sweep can be attained

$$C_{W}^{\max}=P,\qquad C_{L}^{\min}=0,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le P=100 .
$$

With one declaration per side the declaration bracket is

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu}, $$

i.e.

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400, $$

$200$ on the ordinary Tichu scale.

Put the two first places on the losing side.  On the textbook
$+100/+100/0/0$ first-second out convention

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=100+100=200, $$

so that $F_{W}-F_{L}=-200$, the $-200$ first/second out advantage
which is forced on the losing side by $o_{W}=0$.  Hence on the
card+Tichu+out scale

$$
X-Y\le\bigl(C_{W}-C_{L}\bigr)+\bigl(T_{W}-T_{L}\bigr)
      +\bigl(F_{W}-F_{L}\bigr)\le 100+400-200=300 .
$$

The bound is attained for the extremal disposition

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ clean card sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ successful Grand Tichu on the winner,
  $T_{L}=-200$ failed Grand Tichu on the loser,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$, i.e. the losing side is $1^{\rm st}$ and
  $2^{\rm nd}$ out and the winning side is $3^{\rm rd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$
  out,

for which

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

i.e. the familiar $100_{cards}+200_{Grand\,Tichu}$ $300$-point hand on
the $100$-point normalisation.  With the Dragon $5$ and the Mah-Jong
$25$ counted as card material $P=106$ and the same configuration gives
$X_{\max}=306$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y_{\max}=306$, $300$ on the usual
$100$-point normalisation.

If the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ points for winning the hand is written
explicitly in $X$,

$$X_{g}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y_{g}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}, $$

the gross extremum is

$$X_{g}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad Y_{g}^{\min}=0, $$

i.e. $X_{g}-Y_{g}=400$ gross points for the winner against a zero
loser, $250\!-\!(-50)$ on the signed zero-sum $b_{1}=+100,b_{2}=+50,
b_{3}=-50,b_{4}=-100$ convention, the $300$ point net
$100+400-200$ swing which is normally quoted in the literature.
On the international $+100/+50$ first/second out convention
$F_{L}=150$, $F_{W}-F_{L}=-150$, whence

$$X-Y\le100+400-150=350\;{\rm net},\qquad X_{g}-Y_{g}\le450\;{\rm gross}, $$

$285$ points on the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix $C_{W}-C_{L}=35$ special-card
convention, the textbook $100\!+\!200\!-\!200$ ceiling.  This is the
$300$ point net, $400$ point gross with the hand win, $500$ point
gross signed swing which is usually quoted for a third/fourth finishing
winner. ∎

5.text:
In the hand let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$ be the $4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K$ material,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ the going–out bonuses.

On the unsigned teaching book–keeping

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},\qquad
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .
$$

$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$ with equality for the clean sweep
$C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.  On the declaration part

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu},
$$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400$, $200$ for an ordinary Tichu.  On the
$F_{1}=F_{2}=100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ scale the hypothesis
$o_{W}=0$, i.e. the winning side is third and fourth out and the losing
side is first and second out, is

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad F_{W}-F_{L}=-200 .
$$

Hence on the card $+$ Tichu $+$ finish scale

$$
X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le 100+400-200 =300 .
$$

The bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ clean card sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ Grand Tichu made by the winner,
  $T_{L}=-200$ Grand Tichu failed by the loser,
* the loser first and second out, $F_{L}=200$, $F_{W}=0$,

i.e.

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$ points on the usual $100$-point
$5/10/K$ normalisation.  With the Dragon $5$ and the Mahjong $25$
counted as card material the pool is $106$ and the same configuration
gives $X_{\max}=306,\;Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y_{\max}=306$.

In particular with the $100$ point hand win written explicitly,
$X_{g}=100+X$, the gross figure which is normally quoted is

$$
X_{g}^{\max}=100+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad Y_{\min}=0,
$$

i.e. $X_{g}-Y=400$ gross, $500$ points on the symmetric
$b_{1}=b_{2}=+100,\;b_{3}=b_{4}=-100$ zero-sum going-out convention.
On the international $+100/+50$ signed going-out scale
$F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$ and $X_{s}=C_{W}+100+T_{W}+F_{W}$,
$Y_{s}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}$ gives the familiar signed extremum
$X_{s}^{\max}=250,\;Y_{s}^{\min}=-50$, $X_{s}-Y_{s}=300$ net of the
$100$ point win, $400$ points gross.  This is the $100+200-200$
$300$-point hand, $35+400-150=285$ points, $280$ on Phoenix $=0$,
on the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix $C_{W}-C_{L}=35$ special-card
convention. ∎

1.text:
In the usual commercial book keeping let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=P$ be the $5/10/K$ material which can be transferred,
  $P=4(5+10+10)=100$ on the $100$ point normalisation,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses, $T_{W}^{\max }=+200$,
  $T_{L}^{\min }=-200$,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ the going-out bonuses.

On the unsigned card+Tichu+out scale

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},\qquad
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .
$$

A clean sweep is attainable

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}\le P,\qquad C_{W}^{\max }=P,\;C_{L}^{\min }=0,
$$

and on the declaration side

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le T_{W}^{\max }-T_{L}^{\min }=200-(-200)=400,
$$

$200$ for an ordinary Tichu.  The hypothesis $o_{W}=0$ i.e. the
winning side is not first nor second out can be made extremal by
putting the losing side first and second out.  On the symmetric
text book scale

$$
F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\qquad F_{3}=F_{4}=0,
$$

so that in the extremum

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,\qquad
F_{W}-F_{L}=-200 .
$$

Hence on the $P$–point normalisation

$$
X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le P+400-200=300
$$

points on the card+Tichu+out scale.  The bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* $T_{W}=+200$ a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and
  $T_{L}=-200$ a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$, the losing team first and second out and the
  winning team third and fourth out,

i.e.

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300\;{\rm pt}$ is the familiar $100$
point card sweep $+200$ point Grand Tichu swing with the $200$ point
first/second out penalty forced on the loser.  With the $100$ pt hand
win written separately $X_{s}=X+100$ this is the $400$ pt gross
$X_{s}^{\max}=100+100+200$ winner against a $0$ point loser, i.e.
$X_{s}-Y=400$ gross and $X_{s}-Y=450$ gross on the $+100/+50$
first/second out scale, $250-(-50)=300$ net on signed zero–sum
book-keeping.  On the $P=106$ Dragon+Mahjong normalisation this is
$306$ pt net, $300$ pt on the usual $100$ pt normalisation.  In the
Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card only counting $C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}
=35$, $30$ on the Phoenix $=0$ convention, and with the $+100/+50$
finishing scale $F_{L}=150$ the same construction gives the often
quoted

$$
X-Y\le 35+400-150=285\;{\rm pt},
$$

$280$ pt on the Phoenix$=0$ convention, $185$/$180$ pt for an ordinary
Tichu, i.e. the $100_{cards}+200_{GrandTichu}-200_{out}$ $300$ pt
extremum in its usual form. ∎

7.text:
In the unsigned $C+T+F$ book keeping write

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .
$$

On the $56$ card commercial pool

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100,
$$

so that

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100, $$

with equality for the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.
On the one Grand Tichu per side convention

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

so that

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400
$$

$200$ on an ordinary Tichu call.  Put the two first places on the
losing side.  On the symmetric textbook finishing scale
$F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ the hypothesis $o_{W}\ne 1,2$ is

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,
\qquad F_{W}-F_{L}=-200,
$$

the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on the loser.  Hence
on the card$+$Tichu$+$finish scale

$$X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
      \le 100+400-200=300
$$

points.  The bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ a clean card sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and
  $T_{L}=-200$ a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$, i.e. the losing side is $1^{\rm st}$ and
  $2^{\rm nd}$ out and the winning side is $3^{\rm rd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$
  out,

viz.

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0, $$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$ on the $100$ point $5/10/K$ normalisation,
$306$ points on the $100+5+1=106$ point Dragon$+$Mahjong pool.  This is
the familiar $100_{cards}+200_{Grand\,Tichu}$ net hand with the $200$
points of first/second out forced on the loser.

Writing the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ point hand win in $X_{g}$,
$X_{g}=W_{0}+X$, the gross figure which is normally quoted is

$$X_{g}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,
\qquad X_{g}-Y=400,$$

$500$ points gross on the zero-sum $+100/+50/-50/-100$ finishing
convention $F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$.  On the $+100/+50$ first/second out
scale $F_{L}=150$ the net card+Tichu swing is $100+400-150=350$ net of
the $100$ point win, i.e. $450$ points gross, and on the
Mahjong$25$/$Dragon5$/$Phoenix-5$ special-card only accounting
$C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}=35$, $30$ on Phoenix$ =0$,

$$X-Y\le 35+400-150=285,$$

$280$ points on the Phoenix$=0$ convention, $185$/$180$ points for an
ordinary Tichu call, the $35$ point card swing which has to overcome the
$150$ point first/second out advantage of the opponents.  This is the
$300$ point net, $400$ point gross, textbook ceiling for a third/fourth
finishing winner. ∎

2.text:
The points which can be moved from one side to the other in a hand are

* the $5\!-\!10\!-\!J\!-\!Q\!-\!K$ material
 $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$, $C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100$, with equality for the clean
 sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$;
* the Tichu/Grand Tichu declaration.  On the one declaration per side
 convention

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

so that on the declaration part

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400,
$$

$200$ on an ordinary Tichu;
* the going out bonus.  On the text-book first--second out convention
$b_{1}=b_{2}=+100,\;b_{3}=b_{4}=0$ and with the hypothesis $o_{W}=0$

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=b_{1}+b_{2}=200,
\qquad F_{W}-F_{L}=-200,
$$

the losing side being first and second out and the eventual winner
being third and fourth out.  With the $+100/+50$ international

In the unsigned card+Tichu+finish book-keeping

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},

X-Y\le 100+400-200=300,

Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,

so that the net card+Tichu+finish swing of the hand is the familiar

$100_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=300\;{\rm pt}$,

pt first/second out penalty which the slow winner has to overcome.
Writing the obligatory $100$ pt win of the hand explicitly,

X_{s}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,
$$

i.e. $X_{s}-Y=400$ gross, $+400/-0$ signed, for the $100$-point

$$
X-Y\le 35+400-150=285,
$$

public_text.6:
On the 56 card pack the only transferable material is the

$C_{W}+C_{L}=4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K=100$ 

$5/10/K$ points.  In the unsigned book-keeping which is used in the
text books

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}$$

is the card, Tichu and going-out part of the two teams.  On a clean
sweep

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0, $$

and on the Tichu bracket

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu},$$

so that

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400,$$

$200$ for an ordinary Tichu.

On the textbook $+100/+100/0/0$ finishing scale the hypothesis
$o_{W}=0$ is

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=100+100=200 ,$$

i.e. $F_{W}-F_{L}=-200$; the losing side is forced to be first and
second out.  Hence on the card$+$Tichu$+$finish scale

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le 100+400-200=300 $$

and the bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* $T_{W}=+200$ successful Grand Tichu, $T_{L}=-200$ failed Grand
  Tichu,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$,

the winning side being third and fourth out.  In particular

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0, $$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$ points of card$+$Tichu$+$finish is the
usual $100+200$ net swing which has to overcome the $200$ point
first/second out advantage forced on the loser.

With the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ hand win written on the winner this is
the familiar gross figure

$$X^{g}_{ \max}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad Y^{g}_{\min}=0,$$

i.e. $X^{g}-Y^{g}=400$ gross, $500$ points on the signed
$b_{1}=+100,b_{2}=+50,b_{3}=-50,b_{4}=-100$ zero–sum scale.  On the
$+100/+50$ international first/second scale $F_{L}=150$,
$F_{W}-F_{L}=-150$ and the same extremum is $100+400-150=350$ net of
the win bonus, $450$ gross with the $100$ point win, $250-(-50)=300$
signed zero–sum swing.  With the Dragon $5$ and Mah-Jong $25$ counted
as card material the pool is $106$ and the same configuration gives
$X_{\max}=306$, $Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y_{\max}=306$, $406$ gross with the

Mahjong $25$+Dragon $5$+Phoenix $-5$ special-card only version with

public_text.8:
In the ordinary $56$ card book keeping let

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=P$ be the $5/10/K$ material which is taken,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ the finishing bonuses.

On the commercial $P=100$ normalisation

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}\le P ,\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}=P
$$

is the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.  For one declaration per
side

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200
$$

is a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side and a failed Grand
Tichu on the losing side, so that

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400 ,
$$

$200$ on the ordinary Tichu scale.

Put the $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$ places on the losing side.  On the
symmetric text book finishing scale $F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0$
the hypothesis $o_{W}\ne1,2$ is

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200 ,
$$

i.e. $F_{W}-F_{L}=-200$.  On the unsigned card+Tichu+out book
keeping

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad 
Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},
$$

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .
$$

Hence on the $100$ point normalisation

$$
X-Y\le P+400-200=300\;{\rm pt}
$$

and the bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$,
* $T_{W}=+200$ Grand Tichu made, $T_{L}=-200$ Grand Tichu failed,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$,

i.e.

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

so that the net material $+$ Tichu $+$ finishing swing of a
third/fourth finishing winner is the familiar $100+200$ hand.
With the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ point win of the hand written
separately,

$$
X_{g}=W_{0}+X,\qquad Y_{g}=Y,
$$

$$
X_{g}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad Y_{g}^{\min}=0,
$$

the $100_{{\rm win}}+100_{{\rm cards}}+200_{{\rm Grand\;Tichu}}$ gross
maximum which is normally quoted.  On the $106$ point
$5/10/K+$Dragon$+$Mah-Jong pool this is $306$ net, $406$ gross.

In signed zero-sum international book keeping
$F_{1}=+100,\;F_{2}=+50,\;F_{3}=-50,\;F_{4}=-100$ the same extremum is

$$
F_{W}=F_{3}+F_{4}=-150,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=+150,
$$

$F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$, and with the $W_{0}=100$ win kept explicit

$$
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+W_{0}+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le100+100+400-300=300
$$

signed, i.e. $X_{\max}=250,\;Y_{\min}=-50$ on the signed scale and
$X_{g}^{\max}-Y_{g}^{\min}=450$ points gross, $400$ points on the
symmetric $100/100$ finishing convention.  This is the $100+400-200$
text-book ceiling, $285$ points, $280$ points on the Phoenix$=0$
convention, on the Mah-Jong $25$, Dragon $5$, Phoenix $-5$ special-card
only accounting $C_{W}-C_{L}=35$. ∎
public_text.4:
In the signed zero sum book keeping which is used for the hand write

* $C_{W},C_{L}$ the $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ material which finishes on the two
sides $C_{W}+C_{L}=100$,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonus,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ the going out bonus.

On the international scale

$$b_{1}=+100,\;b_{2}=+50,\;b_{3}=-50,\;b_{4}=-100,
\qquad\sum b_{i}=0 , $$

and with $o_{W}=0$ we can put the two first places on the loser

$$F_{W}=b_{3}+b_{4}=-150,\qquad 
F_{L}=b_{1}+b_{2}=+150, $$

so that $F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$.  On the material

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le C_{W}+C_{L}=100,
$$

with equality for the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$.  On the
declaration part

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

Grand Tichu made and Grand Tichu failed, so that

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400,$$
$200$ on the ordinary one-Tichu-per-side convention.

On signed scoring

$$X_{s}=100+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad 
Y_{s}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}, $$

and

$$X_{s}-Y_{s}=100+(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .
\tag{1}$$

Hence in the extremal disposition

$$C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0,\qquad 
T_{W}=+200,\;T_{L}=-200,\qquad 
F_{W}=-150,\;F_{L}=+150, $$

i.e. the winner takes the whole $100$ point pile, makes a Grand Tichu,
fails the opponent's Grand Tichu and is third and fourth out while the
loser is first and second out, we obtain

$$X_{s}^{\max}=100+100+200-150=250,\qquad
Y_{s}^{\min}=0+150-200=-50, $$

and from (1)

$$X_{s}^{\max}-Y_{s}^{\min}=100+100+400-300=300 $$

points net zero sum, the familiar $+300/-300$ swing of the hand.
In the unsigned card+Tichu+finish book keeping $X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}$,
$Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}$ this is

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}=100+200=300,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+150=-50,
$$

$Y_{\min}=0$ on the $F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ unsigned
text-book convention, i.e. the ordinary $300$ point hand

$$X-Y\le(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})\le
100+400-200=300, $$

$X_{\max}=300,\;Y_{\min}=0$ on the $F_{W}=0,F_{L}=200$ textbook scale.
With the $100$ point win of the hand written explicitly in $X$ this is
the often quoted gross

$$X_{\rm gross}^{\max}=100+C_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400, $$

$Y_{\rm gross}^{\min}=0$, $X_{\rm gross}^{\max}-Y_{\rm gross}^{\min}=400$
points gross for the winner, $500$ points gross on the symmetric
$100/100$ first/second convention.

Counting the Dragon $5$ and the Mah Jong $25$ as card material the
pool is $106$ and the same extremum is $X_{\max}=306$, $X-Y_{\max}=306$,
$300$ on the usual $100$ point normalisation.  On the special-card-only
Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix convention $C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}=35$, $30$ on
Phoenix$=0$, and with $F_{L}=150$ the Grand-Tichu extremum gives the
text-book

$$X-Y\le35+400-150=285,\qquad 280\;{\rm on\;Phoenix}=0, $$

$185/180$ points for an ordinary Tichu.  This is the $100+200-200$
$300$ point net, $400$ point gross ceiling normally quoted for a
third/fourth finishing winner. ∎

$$

On the 56 card pack

and the clean sweep can be attained

$$

T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu}, $$

Put the two first places on the losing side.  On the textbook

$100+400-200$ swing which is normally quoted in the literature.

Xs−Ys =100+100+400−300=300, gross unsigned Xg−Yg=450.

Special-card-only version persists: Cw−Clmax=35, 30 on Phoenix=0,
F L=150 on +100/+50 scale → X−Y ≤35+400−150=285, 280 on Phoenix=0,
185/180 for ordinary Tichu. This is Colleague 1’s figure and is internally
consistent once the card pool is restricted to Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix.

Unresolved convention points that still move the number:
whether the 100 pt win bonus is included in X, whether go-out is
+100/+100/0/0 unsigned or +100/+50/−50/−100 signed, whether Dragon/Mahjong
are counted in the 100 pt card pool, and whether Y is allowed negative after
a failed Grand Tichu.

Current belief: the textbook zero-win-bonus net maximum under the usual
100-pt 5/10/K pool with Grand Tichu both sides and winning team third/fourth
is 300 pts, 306 pts with Dragon+Mahjong, i.e. 100 card +400 Tichu −200 go-out.
With the 100 pt win bonus written explicitly this is the familiar 400 pt
gross maximum, 450 pt gross on the +100/+50 convention, 285/280 pts on the
Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card-only accounting. Convergence in round 2
is to the 300 net/400 gross textbook figure; Colleague 1 remains the outlier
on special-card accounting.
reflection_text.1:
The current round is a near-consensus restatement of the book-keeping extremum.

Core decomposition on signed scoring

X_s = W0 + Cw + Tw + Fw ,   Y_s = Cl + Tl + Fl
X_s – Y_s = W0 + (Cw–Cl) + (Tw–Tl) + (Fw–Fl)

with W0 = 100 for winning the hand.  On the unsigned C+T+F scale
X = Cw + Tw + Fw , Y = Cl + Tl + Fl , X–Y = (Cw–Cl)+(Tw–Tl)+(Fw–Fl).

Card pool
* 5/10/K commercial pool P=100, clean sweep Cw–Cl =100, attainable.
* P=106 with Dragon 5 + Mahjong 1.
* Special-card only Mahjong 25 + Dragon 5 + Phoenix –5 gives Cw–Cl max =35, 30 on Phoenix=0 convention.

Declarations
Tw max = +200 Grand Tichu made, Tl min = –200 Grand Tichu failed.
Tw–Tl =400, 200 for an ordinary Tichu.

Finishing under the hypothesis oW≠1,2, extremal oL =1,2, oW =3,4
* Zero-sum international b1=+100,b2=+50,b3=–50,b4=–100
  Fw = –150 , Fl = +150 , Fw–Fl = –300.
* Textbook unsigned b1=b2=+100,b3=b4=0
  Fw =0 , Fl =200 , Fw–Fl = –200.
* International unsigned +100/+50
  Fw = –150 , Fl = +150 , Fw–Fl = –300, Fl=150 on unsigned +100/+50/0/0.

Extremal values
Commercial P=100, Grand Tichu
* Zero-sum signed with W0 explicit:
  X_s max =100+100+200–150=250 , Y_s min =0–200+150=–50
  X_s – Y_s =100+100+400–300=300 net signed swing.
  Unsigned C+T+F: Xmax=100+200=300, Ymin=0, X–Y=300.
* Unsigned textbook Fw=0,Fl=200:
  Xmax =Cw+Tw+Fw=100+200=300 , Ymin=Cl+Tl+Fl=0–200+200=0
  X–Y=300.  With W0 written in X, Xg max=100+100+200=400, Ymin=0,
  Xg–Y=400 gross, the 100+200–200 hand usually quoted.
* +100/+50 finishing: Fw–Fl=–150, X–Y ≤100+400–150=350 net of W0,
  450 gross with W0.  Signed zero-sum gives the same 300 net.

Special-card convention
Cw–Cl max=35, 30 Phoenix=0, with +100/+50 finishing Fl=150
X–Y ≤35+400–150=285, 280 on Phoenix=0, 185/180 for ordinary Tichu.
That is the 35-point card swing quoted in round 0.

What remains unresolved
* Whether W0=100 is counted inside X in the statement “winning team gets X points”.
* Zero-sum vs unsigned finishing: b3,b4 negative vs zero, and b2=50 vs 100.
* Card pool definition: 100-point 5/10/K vs 106 with Dragon/Mahjong vs special-card only Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix.
The 300-point net, 400-point gross, 285/280-point special-card figures are the same extremum under those conventions. The textbook zero-win-bonus zero-sum statement is the familiar 100card+200GrandTichu–200out =300 point hand with the winner third/fourth out.

3.text:
On the unsigned $C+T+F$ book-keeping that is used in the textbooks

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
$$

let $P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100$ be the $5/10/K$ material.
A clean sweep can be attained

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}\le P,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=P,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0,
$$

and with one declaration per side

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu},
$$

so that

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400,
$$

$200$ on an ordinary Tichu.

Let $o_{W}=0$, i.e. the winning side is not $1^{\rm st}$ nor $2^{\rm nd}$
out.  On the textbook symmetric finishing scale
$F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ the extremum is obtained by putting
the two first places on the loser,

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,\qquad 
F_{W}-F_{L}=-200 .
$$

Hence on the card$+$Tichu$+$finish scale

$$
X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le P+400-200=100+400-200=300
$$

points.  The bound is attained for the familiar extremal hand

* $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$ clean card sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ successful Grand Tichu on the winner,
  $T_{L}=-200$ failed Grand Tichu on the loser,
* $F_{W}=0$, $F_{L}=200$, the loser is $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$ out
  and the winner is $3^{\rm rd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out,

for which

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$ pt is the $100_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm
Grand\,Tichu}$ net swing that has to overcome the forced $200$ pt
first$/$second out advantage of the loser.  With the Dragon $5$ and
Mah-Jong $25$ counted as card material $P=106$ this is $306$ pt net,
$306$ pt $=100+200$ net on the usual $100$ pt normalisation.

Writing the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ pt hand win explicitly in the
winner’s score,
$X_{g}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}$, $Y_{g}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}$,
the gross figure normally quoted is

$$
X_{g}^{\max}=W_{0}+P+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
Y_{g}^{\min}=0,
$$

i.e. $X_{g}-Y_{g}=400$ gross, $400$ pt $=100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm cards}
+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$, the $250$ $-(-50)=300$ pt signed zero–sum
swing on the $b_{1}=+100,b_{2}=+50,b_{3}=-50,b_{4}=-100$ international
scale.  On the $+100/+50$ first$/$second out scale $F_{L}=150$,
$F_{W}-F_{L}=-150$, the usual textbook net figures become
$100+400-150=350$ net, $450$ gross with the hand win, and $35+400-150
=285$ pt, $280$ pt on the Phoenix$=0$ convention, on the
Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card only accounting.  This is the
$100+400-200$ $300$ pt net, $400$ pt gross, ceiling for a third/fourth
finishing winner. ∎

6.text:
In the $C+T+F$ book keeping put

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}
\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) $$

on the unsigned points–won/points–lost scale.  On the 56 card pack

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100$$

so that a clean sweep can be attained

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0 .$$

With one declaration per side

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,$$

Grand Tichu made on the winner and Grand Tichu failed on the loser, so
that on the declaration part

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400,$$
$200$ on an ordinary Tichu.

Let $o_{W}=0$ be the hypothesis that the winning side is not first nor
second out.  On the symmetric teaching finishing scale
$F_{1}=F_{2}=+100$, $F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ the extremal disposition is the two
first places on the loser,

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,\qquad F_{W}-F_{L}=-200,$$

so that the $200$ points of first/second out are forced on the losing
side.  Hence on the card$+$Tichu$+$finish scale

$$X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
      \le 100+400-200=300 $$

points.  The bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ the clean $5/10/K$ sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ a successful Grand Tichu on the winner,
  $T_{L}=-200$ a failed Grand Tichu on the loser,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$, the loser $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$ out
  and the winner $3^{\rm rd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out,

i.e.

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,$$

so that the net card$+$Tichu$+$finish swing of a third/fourth finishing
winner is the familiar

$$100_{{\rm cards}}+200_{{\rm Grand\,Tichu}}-200_{{\rm out}}=300 $$

points.  Writing the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ point hand win explicitly in
the winner's score, $X_{g}=W_{0}+X$,

$$X_{g}^{\max}=100+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+100+200=400,\qquad 
Y_{g}^{\min}=0, $$

i.e. $X_{g}-Y=400$ gross, $300$ net of the $100$ point win, the
$100_{win}+100_{cards}+200_{Grand Tichu}$ hand which is normally quoted
for a winner who is forced to finish third and fourth.  With the
Dragon $5$ and Mah-Jong $25$ counted the pool is $P=106$ and the same
construction gives $X_{\max}=306$, $X_{g}^{\max}=406$, $X-Y=306$ net,
$406$ gross.  On the international $+100/+50$ signed finishing scale
$F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$ the signed zero-sum swing is the same $300$ points
net, $X_{s}^{\max}=250$, $Y_{s}^{\min}=-50$, $X_{s}-Y_{s}=300$, i.e.
$450$ points gross with the $100$ point win.  The $285$, $280$ on
Phoenix$=0$, figure is the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card only
$C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}=35$ version. ∎

8.text:
On the unsigned $C+T+F$ book keeping write

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})  $$

on the $56$ card commercial pool

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100,$$
so that with a clean sweep

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100 ,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0,$$

and on one declaration per side

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu}, $$

i.e.

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400, $$

$200$ on the ordinary Tichu scale.  Put the two first places on the
losing side.  On the text book $F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0$
finishing scale the hypothesis $o_{W}=0$, i.e. the winner is third and
fourth out, is

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,\qquad 
F_{W}-F_{L}=-200 ,$$

the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on the loser.  Hence
on the card+Tichu+finish scale

$$X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
      \le 100+400-200=300 $$

and the bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ the clean $5/10/K$ sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ a successful Grand Tichu on the winner and
  $T_{L}=-200$ a failed Grand Tichu on the loser,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$, the loser first and second out and the winner
  third and fourth out,

i.e.

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0, $$

so that the net card+Tichu+finish swing of a third/fourth finishing
winner is the familiar $100_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm GrandTichu}$ $300$
point hand.  With the Dragon $5$ and the Mah-Jong $25$ counted as card
material $P=106$ this is $306$ net.

Writing the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ point hand win explicitly,
$X_{g}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}$, $Y_{g}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}$,

$$X_{g}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad Y_{g}^{\min}=0,$$
i.e. $X_{g}-Y_{g}=400$ gross on the $F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,F_{3}=F_{4}=0$
scale, $450$ gross on the $+100/+50$ international zero-sum scale.
In signed zero-sum book keeping this is the familiar $250-(-50)=300$
net swing, $X_{s}^{\max}=250$, $Y_{s}^{\min}=-50$, of the hand.  This
is $100+200-200$ on the usual $100$ point normalisation, $285$ points,
$280$ on the Phoenix$=0$ convention, on the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix
special-card only $C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}=35$ accounting. ∎

4.text:
In the hand write on the unsigned card + Tichu + finishing scale

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}, $$

so that

$$X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .$$

On the 56-card commercial pool

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K=100 , $$

so that on a clean sweep

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0, $$

is attainable.  With one declaration per side

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200\ {\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\ {\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu}, $$

hence

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400, $$

$200$ on an ordinary Tichu.

Put the two first places on the losing side.  On the textbook
$F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ finishing scale the hypothesis
$o_{W}=0$, i.e. the winning side is third and fourth out, is

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,\qquad 
F_{W}-F_{L}=-200, $$

the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on the loser. Hence
on the card $+$ Tichu $+$ finish scale

$$X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le 100+400-200=300 $$

points.  The bound is attained for the extremal disposition

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ clean card sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ a successful Grand Tichu on the winner and
  $T_{L}=-200$ a failed Grand Tichu on the loser,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$ the loser first and second out and the winner
  third and fourth out,

i.e.

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$ pt is the familiar
$100_{{\rm cards}}+200_{{\rm Grand\,Tichu}}$ net swing which has to
overcome the $200$ pt first/second out penalty forced on the loser.
With the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ pt hand win written explicitly in the
winner's score $X_{g}=W_{0}+X$,

$$X_{g}^{\max}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad Y_{\min}=0, $$

i.e. $X_{g}-Y=400$ gross, $100+100+200-200$, the $400$ pt gross
$100_{{\rm win}}+100_{{\rm cards}}+200_{{\rm Grand\,Tichu}}$ hand
normally quoted for a third/fourth finishing winner.  On the signed
zero-sum $b_{1}=+100,b_{2}=+50,b_{3}=-50,b_{4}=-100$ international
finishing scale this is $F_{W}=-150,F_{L}=+150$, $F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$,
$X_{s}^{\max}=250,\;Y_{s}^{\min}=-50$ and $X_{s}-Y_{s}=300$ net zero-sum,
$400$ pt gross with the $100$ pt win written in $X$.  The $P=106$
Dragon+Mahjong normalisation is $306$ net, $406$ gross, and on the
Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card only convention $C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}
=35$, $30$ on Phoenix$=0$, $F_{L}=150$ on the $+100/+50$ scale,
$X-Y\le35+400-150=285$, $280$ on Phoenix$=0$, the usual $100+200-200$
text-book ceiling. ∎

2.text:
In the unsigned card-Tichu-finish book keeping put

$$
X_{0}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y_{0}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},
$$

so that on a hand

$$
X_{0}-Y_{0}=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .
$$

$C_{W}+C_{L}=P$ is the $5\!-\!10\!-\!K$ material.  On the 100 pt
normalisation $P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100$ and the clean sweep is
attainable

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}\le P,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=P,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0 .
$$

With one declaration per side

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu},
$$

hence

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400,
$$

$200$ for an ordinary Tichu.

Let $o_{W}=0$ be the condition that the winning side does not take the
first two places.  On the symmetric textbook finishing scale

$$
F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\qquad F_{3}=F_{4}=0,
$$

the extremal disposition is the loser first and second and the winner
third and fourth,

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,\qquad 
F_{W}-F_{L}=-200 .
$$

Hence on the $C+T+F$ net scale

$$
X_{0}-Y_{0}\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
        \le P+400-200=300
$$

points.  The bound is attained for the extremum

* $C_{W}=P=100,\;C_{L}=0$  clean card sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ successful Grand Tichu on the winner,
  $T_{L}=-200$ failed Grand Tichu on the loser,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$, i.e. the loser is $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$
  out and the winner is $3^{\rm rd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out,

for which

$$
X_{0}^{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{0}^{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

i.e. the familiar $100_{{\rm cards}}+200_{{\rm Grand\,Tichu}}$ net hand
with the $200$ pt first/second out penalty forced on the loser.

Writing the obligatory $W_{0}=100$ pt hand win on the winner,
$X=W_{0}+X_{0},\;Y=Y_{0}$, the gross scores which are normally quoted
are

$$
X^{\max}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
Y^{\min}=0,
$$

so that

$$
X^{\max}-Y^{\min}=400
$$

gross, $300$ net of the $100$ pt win, $X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{0}^{\min}=300$ on
the $C+T+F$ scale.  With the Dragon $5$ and the Mah Jong $25$ counted
the pool is $P=106$ and the same configuration gives $X_{0}^{\max}=306$,
$X^{\max}=406$, $X-Y_{\max}=306$ net, $406$ gross.  On the
international signed $b_{1}=+100,b_{2}=+50,b_{3}=-50,b_{4}=-100$
scale $F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$ and $X-Y=W_{0}+(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+
(F_{W}-F_{L})\le100+100+400-300=300$ signed, i.e. $X^{\max}=250$,
$Y^{\min}=-50$.  This is the $100+200-200$ textbook ceiling.  On the
Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card only convention $C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}
=35$, $30$ on Phoenix$=0$, and with $F_{L}=150$ this is the often quoted
$35+400-150=285$, $280$ on Phoenix$=0$, $185/180$ for an ordinary
Tichu, i.e. the $300$ pt net, $400$ pt gross, third/fourth-finishing
extremum. ∎

1.text:
On the $C+T+F$ book keeping which is normally used for the hand put

* $C_{W}+C_{L}=P$ for the $5/10/K$ material,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the Tichu / Grand Tichu bonus,
* $F_{W},F_{L}$ for the going-out bonus,

$$

$$

$$

$$

declaration per side

$$

\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400,
$$

$200$ on an ordinary Tichu.  Put the two first places on the loser.
On the text-book $F_{1}=F_{2}=100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ scale the hypothesis
$o_{W}\ne1,2$, i.e. the winner is third and fourth out, is

$$

Hence on the card$+$Tichu$+$finish scale

$$

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ clean card sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ a successful Grand Tichu on the winner and
  $T_{L}=-200$ a failed Grand Tichu on the loser,

for which

$$
X_{0}^{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{0}^{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,

so that on the usual $C+T+F$ scale the net swing of the hand is the
familiar

$$
100_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}=300\;{\rm pt},
$$

the $200$ pt first/second out advantage being forced on the loser.
Writing the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ pt hand win on the winner,
$X_{g}=W_{0}+X_{0}$, $Y_{g}=Y_{0}$, this is the textbook gross
extremum

$$

\qquad Y_{g}^{\min}=0,
$$

i.e. $X_{g}-Y_{g}=400$ pt gross for the winner against a zero loser,

7.text:
On the unsigned card $+$ Tichu $+$ finish book keeping put

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},
\qquad X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) ,$$

and let $o_{W}=0$ be the hypothesis that the winning side is not
$1^{\rm st}$ or $2^{\rm nd}$ out.  In the extremum we can put the two
first places on the loser.

* Card material.  On the commercial $5/10/K$ normalisation

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100 ,\qquad
C_{W}-C_{L}\le P,$$

with the clean sweep $C_{W}=P,\;C_{L}=0$ attainable.

* Declarations.  With one declaration per side

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=-200{\rm \;failed\;Grand\;Tichu}, $$

so that

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400,$$

$200$ on an ordinary Tichu.

* Finish.  On the symmetric text book scale
$F_{1}=F_{2}=+100$, $F_{3}=F_{4}=0$,

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,\qquad
F_{W}-F_{L}=-200 ,$$

the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on the losing side by
$o_{W}=0$.  On the $+100/+50$ international zero-sum scale this is
$F_{W}=-150$, $F_{L}=+150$, $F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$.

Hence on the $P$-point card+Tichu+finish scale

$$X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
      \le P+400-200 .$$

For the usual $P=100$ $5/10/K$ normalisation this is the familiar

$$X-Y\le 100+400-200=300$$

points on the card+Tichu+finish scale, and the bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ clean card sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ successful Grand Tichu on the winner,
  $T_{L}=-200$ failed Grand Tichu on the loser,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$ the loser $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$ out,
  the winner $3^{\rm rd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out,

i.e.

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0, $$

so that the net card$+$Tichu$+$finish swing of a third/fourth finishing
winner is the $100_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$ $300$-point hand
which has to overcome the $200$-point first/second out penalty forced
on the loser.

Writing the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ points for winning the hand in
$X_{g}=W_{0}+X$ the gross figure which is normally quoted is

$$X_{g}^{\max}=100+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad Y_{\min}=0,
\qquad X_{g}-Y=400,$$

$500$ points gross on the signed $b_{1}=+100,b_{2}=+50,b_{3}=-50,
b_{4}=-100$ zero-sum convention.  With the Dragon $5$ and the Mahjong
$25$ counted as card material $P=106$ and the same extremum gives

$$X_{\max}=306,\;Y_{\min}=0,\;X-Y_{\max}=306\ {\rm net},
\qquad X_{g}^{\max}=406\ {\rm gross},$$

the $300$/$400$ figure being the $100$-point normalisation quoted in
the literature.  On the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card only
accounting $C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}=35$, $30$ on the Phoenix$=0$ convention,
and with the $+100/+50$ finishing scale $F_{L}=150$, the same
construction gives the often quoted
$X-Y\le 35+400-150=285$ pt, $280$ pt on the Phoenix$=0$ convention,
$185$/$180$ pt for an ordinary Tichu, i.e. the $100+200-200$ textbook
ceiling. ∎

5.text:
On the unsigned card + Tichu + finishing scale

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
$$

let $P$ be the transferable $5/10/K$ material. On the commercial
normalisation

$$
C_{W}+C_{L}=P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100,
\qquad C_{W}-C_{L}\le P ,
$$

with equality for the clean sweep $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$. With one
declaration per side

$$
T_{W}^{\max }=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min }=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu},
\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400,
$$

$200$ on an ordinary Tichu.  Put the first two places on the loser.
On the text book $F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ finishing scale and
$o_{W}=0$,

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,\qquad 
F_{W}-F_{L}=-200,
$$

the $-200$ first/second out advantage being forced on the loser by
the hypothesis that the eventual winner is $3^{\rm rd}/4^{\rm th}$ out.
Hence on the card+Tichu+finish scale

$$
X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le P+400-200 .
$$

For $P=100$

$$
X-Y\le 100+400-200=300
$$

and the bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ clean card sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ a successful Grand Tichu on the winner and
  $T_{L}=-200$ a failed Grand Tichu on the loser,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$, i.e. the loser is $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$
  out and the winner is $3^{\rm rd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out,

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

the familiar $100_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm Grand Tichu}$ net hand with the
$200$ point first/second out penalty forced on the loser.  With the
obligatory $W_{0}=100$ point hand win written explicitly in $X$,

$$
X_{g}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y_{g}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},
$$

$$
X_{g}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad Y_{g}^{\min}=0,
$$

i.e. $X_{g}-Y_{g}=400$ gross for the $100$ point $5/10/K$
normalisation, $306$ net and $406$ gross on the $P=106$
Dragon $5+$ Mahjong $25$ pool.  On the signed zero-sum
$b_{1}=+100,b_{2}=+50,b_{3}=-50,b_{4}=-100$ scale this is the
$X_{s}^{\max}=250,\;Y_{s}^{\min}=-50$, $X_{s}-Y_{s}=300$ net,
$450$ gross with the $100$ point win, swing, i.e. the $100+400-200$
text book ceiling normally quoted for a third/fourth finishing winner.
The $35$ point Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card version is
$35+400-150=285$, $280$ on Phoenix$=0$, $185/180$ for an ordinary
Tichu, the $100+200-200$ $300$ point net ceiling in its usual form. ∎

public_text.3:
On the unsigned $C+T+F$ book-keeping that is used in the textbooks

$$
X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L},\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
$$

let $P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100$ be the $5/10/K$ material.
A clean sweep can be attained

$$
C_{W}-C_{L}\le P,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=P,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0,
$$

and with one declaration per side

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu},
$$

so that

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400,
$$

$200$ on an ordinary Tichu.

Let $o_{W}=0$, i.e. the winning side is not $1^{\rm st}$ nor $2^{\rm nd}$
out.  On the textbook symmetric finishing scale
$F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ the extremum is obtained by putting
the two first places on the loser,

$$
F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,\qquad 
F_{W}-F_{L}=-200 .
$$

Hence on the card$+$Tichu$+$finish scale

$$
X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
     \le P+400-200=100+400-200=300
$$

points.  The bound is attained for the familiar extremal hand

* $C_{W}=100$, $C_{L}=0$ clean card sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ successful Grand Tichu on the winner,
  $T_{L}=-200$ failed Grand Tichu on the loser,
* $F_{W}=0$, $F_{L}=200$, the loser is $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$ out
  and the winner is $3^{\rm rd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out,

for which

$$
X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,
$$

so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$ pt is the $100_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm
Grand\,Tichu}$ net swing that has to overcome the forced $200$ pt
first$/$second out advantage of the loser.  With the Dragon $5$ and
Mah-Jong $25$ counted as card material $P=106$ this is $306$ pt net,
$306$ pt $=100+200$ net on the usual $100$ pt normalisation.

Writing the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ pt hand win explicitly in the
winner’s score,
$X_{g}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}$, $Y_{g}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}$,
the gross figure normally quoted is

$$
X_{g}^{\max}=W_{0}+P+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
Y_{g}^{\min}=0,
$$

i.e. $X_{g}-Y_{g}=400$ gross, $400$ pt $=100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm cards}
+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$, the $250$ $-(-50)=300$ pt signed zero–sum
swing on the $b_{1}=+100,b_{2}=+50,b_{3}=-50,b_{4}=-100$ international
scale.  On the $+100/+50$ first$/$second out scale $F_{L}=150$,
$F_{W}-F_{L}=-150$, the usual textbook net figures become
$100+400-150=350$ net, $450$ gross with the hand win, and $35+400-150
=285$ pt, $280$ pt on the Phoenix$=0$ convention, on the
Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card only accounting.  This is the
$100+400-200$ $300$ pt net, $400$ pt gross, ceiling for a third/fourth
finishing winner. ∎
public_text.6:
In the $C+T+F$ book keeping put

$$X=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}\qquad Y=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}
\qquad 
X-Y=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) $$

on the unsigned points–won/points–lost scale.  On the 56 card pack

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100$$

so that a clean sweep can be attained

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le 100,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0 .$$

With one declaration per side

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,$$

Grand Tichu made on the winner and Grand Tichu failed on the loser, so
that on the declaration part

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400,$$
$200$ on an ordinary Tichu.

Let $o_{W}=0$ be the hypothesis that the winning side is not first nor
second out.  On the symmetric teaching finishing scale
$F_{1}=F_{2}=+100$, $F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ the extremal disposition is the two
first places on the loser,

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,\qquad F_{W}-F_{L}=-200,$$

so that the $200$ points of first/second out are forced on the losing
side.  Hence on the card$+$Tichu$+$finish scale

$$X-Y\le (C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})
      \le 100+400-200=300 $$

points.  The bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ the clean $5/10/K$ sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ a successful Grand Tichu on the winner,
  $T_{L}=-200$ a failed Grand Tichu on the loser,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$, the loser $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$ out
  and the winner $3^{\rm rd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out,

i.e.

$$X_{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,$$

so that the net card$+$Tichu$+$finish swing of a third/fourth finishing
winner is the familiar

$$100_{{\rm cards}}+200_{{\rm Grand\,Tichu}}-200_{{\rm out}}=300 $$

points.  Writing the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ point hand win explicitly in
the winner's score, $X_{g}=W_{0}+X$,

$$X_{g}^{\max}=100+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+100+200=400,\qquad 
Y_{g}^{\min}=0, $$

i.e. $X_{g}-Y=400$ gross, $300$ net of the $100$ point win, the
$100_{win}+100_{cards}+200_{Grand Tichu}$ hand which is normally quoted
for a winner who is forced to finish third and fourth.  With the
Dragon $5$ and Mah-Jong $25$ counted the pool is $P=106$ and the same
construction gives $X_{\max}=306$, $X_{g}^{\max}=406$, $X-Y=306$ net,
$406$ gross.  On the international $+100/+50$ signed finishing scale
$F_{W}-F_{L}=-300$ the signed zero-sum swing is the same $300$ points
net, $X_{s}^{\max}=250$, $Y_{s}^{\min}=-50$, $X_{s}-Y_{s}=300$, i.e.
$450$ points gross with the $100$ point win.  The $285$, $280$ on
Phoenix$=0$, figure is the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix special-card only
$C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}=35$ version. ∎

X_{0}^{\max}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+200+0=300,\qquad
Y_{0}^{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0,

$$

$$

\qquad Y_{g}^{\min}=0,

  Fw=0 , Fl=200 , Fw-Fl = -200.

  Fw=-150 , Fl=+150 , Fw-Fl = -300.

4.text:
On the unsigned card+Tichu+finish book keeping

$$X_{0}=C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W},\qquad Y_{0}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}$$

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}=(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L}) .$$

For the commercial $5/10/K$ material

$$C_{W}+C_{L}=P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100 ,$$

so that a clean sweep can be attained

$$C_{W}-C_{L}\le P,\qquad C_{W}^{\max}=100,\;C_{L}^{\min}=0 .$$

With one declaration per side

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu},\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu},$$

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le200-(-200)=400,$$

$200$ for an ordinary Tichu.

Put the two first places on the loser.  On the textbook unsigned
finish scale $F_{1}=F_{2}=+100,\;F_{3}=F_{4}=0$ the hypothesis
$o_{W}\ne1,2$, i.e. the winner is third and fourth out, is

$$F_{W}=0,\qquad F_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200,\qquad 
F_{W}-F_{L}=-200.$$

Hence on the $C+T+F$ scale

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}\le P+400-200=100+400-200=300 $$

points and the bound is attained for

* $C_{W}=100,\;C_{L}=0$ clean $5/10/K$ sweep,
* $T_{W}=+200$ successful Grand Tichu on the winner,
  $T_{L}=-200$ failed Grand Tichu on the loser,
* $F_{W}=0,\;F_{L}=200$, loser $1^{\rm st}$ and $2^{\rm nd}$ out,
  winner $3^{\rm rd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out,

$$X_{0}^{\max}=100+200+0=300,\qquad 
Y_{0}^{\min}=0-200+200=0, $$

the familiar $100_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm Grand\;Tichu}$ net hand which
has to overcome the forced $200$ pt first/second out advantage of the
loser.

Writing the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ pt hand win explicitly in the
winner’s score $X_{g}=W_{0}+X_{0}$, $Y_{g}=Y_{0}$,

$$X_{g}^{\max}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad Y_{g}^{\min}=0,$$

i.e. $X_{g}-Y_{g}=400$ gross for the $100$-point $5/10/K$
normalisation, $300$ net of the $100$ pt win.  On the signed zero-sum
$b_{1}=+100,b_{2}=+50,b_{3}=-50,b_{4}=-100$ international scale this is
$X_{s}^{\max}=250,\;Y_{s}^{\min}=-50$, $X_{s}-Y_{s}=300$ net, $450$
gross with the win written in $X$.

With the Dragon $5$ and Mah-Jong $25$ counted as card material
$P=106$ the same extremum is $X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{0}^{\min}=306$ net,
$X_{g}^{\max}-Y_{g}^{\min}=406$ gross, the $300/400$ figure being the
usual $P=100$ textbook ceiling.  On the Mahjong/Dragon/Phoenix
special-card-only convention $C_{W}-C_{L}^{\max}=35$, $30$ on
Phoenix$=0$, and with the $+100/+50$ finish scale $F_{L}=150$ this is
the quoted $35+400-150=285$, $280$ on Phoenix$=0$, $185/180$ for an
ordinary Tichu, i.e. the $100+200-200$ textbook $300$ pt net,
$400$ pt gross, third/fourth-finishing extremum.

so that

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le200-(-200)=400, $$

$$X_{0}-Y_{0}\le(C_{W}-C_{L})+(T_{W}-T_{L})+(F_{W}-F_{L})

points.  The bound is attained for the extremal hand

  $T_{L}=-200$ a failed Grand Tichu on the loser,

Y_{0}^{\min}=C_{L}+T_{L}+F_{L}=0-200+200=0, $$

which has to overcome the forced $200$ pt first/second out advantage of
the loser.  With the compulsory $W_{0}=100$ pt hand win written
explicitly in the winner’s score $X_{g}=W_{0}+X_{0}$,

$$X_{g}^{\max}=W_{0}+C_{W}+T_{W}+F_{W}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad Y_{g}^{\min}=0,
$$

so that $X_{g}-Y_{g}=400$ pt gross, $300$ pt net of the $100$ pt win,
is the textbook $100_{\rm win}+100_{\rm cards}+200_{\rm Grand\;Tichu}$
maximum for a third/fourth finishing winner.  With the Dragon $5$ and
Mah-Jong $25$ counted $P=106$ this is $X_{0}-Y_{0}=306$ net, $X_{g}-
Y_{g}=406$ gross.  On the signed $b_{1}=+100,b_{2}=+50,b_{3}=-50,b_{4}=-
100$ international scale this is the $250-(-50)=300$ pt signed net
swing, $450$ pt gross with the $100$ pt win written explicitly. ∎

 T_{L}^{\min}=-200\;{\rm failed\;Grand\;Tichu}, $$
